Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 5, verse 1 (part 1 of 2):

(Surat al-Ma'idah)
Madaniyyah, except for verse 3. It was revealed at ʿArafat during the Farewell Pilgrimage. Its verses number 120. It was revealed after the Conquest.

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿O you who have believed, fulfil the contracts.﴾

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿O you who have believed, fulfil the contracts.﴾ In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: It is said: wafā bil-ʿahd and awfā bihi (he fulfilled the covenant). From this is the verse ﴿And those who fulfil their covenant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177]. The ʿaqd (contract) is the joining of one thing to another in a manner of firm binding and securing. The ʿahd (covenant) is an obligation, and the ʿaqd is a commitment in a manner of firm binding. Since faith (īmān) is an expression for the knowledge of Allah, the Exalted, in His essence, His attributes, His rulings and His acts, and since among His rulings is that it is obligatory upon all creation to show submission to Allah, the Exalted, in all His obligations, commands and prohibitions, this contract is one of the matters required for the realization of the reality of faith. Therefore He said: ﴿O you who have believed, fulfil the contracts.﴾ That is, O you who have committed yourselves by your faith to various kinds of contracts and covenants in showing obedience to Allah, fulfil those contracts. Allah, the Exalted, named these obligations "contracts," as in this verse, because He has bound them to His servants, just as one thing is tied to another with a strong rope.

Know that He, the Exalted, sometimes calls these obligations "contracts," as in this verse and as in His saying: ﴿But He will hold you accountable for the oaths you have sworn firmly﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 89]. And sometimes "covenants," as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And fulfil My covenant; I will fulfil your covenant﴾ [al-Baqarah: 40], and He said: ﴿And fulfil the covenant of Allah when you have pledged, and do not break the oaths after their confirmation﴾ [al-Nahl: 91]. The essential meaning of this verse is that He commanded the fulfilment of the obligations, both by doing and by abstaining.

The second issue: al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: If one vows to fast on the day of ʿId, or vows to slaughter his son, the vow is void. Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Rather, it is valid.

The argument of Abu Hanifah is that he vowed the fast and the slaughter, so the fast and the slaughter become obligatory upon him. The explanation of the first: he vowed to fast on the day of ʿId and vowed to slaughter the son. The fast of the ʿId is a compound reality made up of the fast and its occurrence on the day of ʿId; likewise, slaughtering the son is a compound reality made up of the slaughter and its occurrence upon the son. Whoever performs a compound performs each of its two components. Therefore, one who commits himself to fasting on the day of ʿId and slaughtering the son necessarily commits himself to the fast and the slaughter.

Having established this, we say: it is necessary that the fast and the slaughter be obligatory upon him, due to His saying: ﴿Fulfil the contracts﴾ and His saying: ﴿Why do you say what you do not do?﴾ [al-Saff: 2], and His saying: ﴿They fulfil the vow﴾ [al-Insan: 7], and His saying, upon him be blessings and peace: "Fulfil your vow." The most that can be said is that this vow is void with respect to the specific matter that the fast falls on the day of ʿId and that the slaughter falls on the son; but the general text after specification remains a valid proof.

The argument of al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, is that this is a vow in disobedience, so it is void, due to his saying, upon him be blessings and peace: "There is no vow in disobedience to Allah."

The third issue: Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the option of the session (khiyar al-majlis) is not established. Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is established.

The argument of Abu Hanifah is that when the sale and purchase have been concluded, it is necessary that cancellation be prohibited, due to the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Fulfil the contracts.﴾

The argument of al-Shafiʿi is that he restricts this generality by the report, which is his saying, upon him be blessings and peace: "The two parties to a sale have the option, each of them, as long as they have not separated."

The fourth issue: Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, said: combining the divorces (talaq) together is forbidden, and al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is not forbidden.

The argument of Abu Hanifah is that marriage is one of the contracts, due to the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And do not determine to conclude the marriage tie﴾ [al-Baqarah: 235]. So it is necessary that its dissolution be prohibited, due to the saying of the Exalted: ﴿Fulfil the contracts.﴾ The application of this has been abandoned concerning a single pronouncement by consensus, so it remains upon the original ruling regarding what lies beyond it. Al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, restricted this generality by analogy, which is that if combining were forbidden it would not take effect, and it does take effect, so it is not forbidden.

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock.﴾

Know that when the Exalted, by the first verse, established for all the responsible that it is obligatory upon them to submit to all the obligations of Allah, the Exalted, which is like the universal principle and the excellent rule, He then began to mention the detailed obligations, so He began with mentioning what is lawful and what is unlawful of foods, and He said: ﴿Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock.﴾ In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: They said: every living thing that has no intellect is a bahimah (beast), from the expression istabhama al-amr ʿala fulan, when the matter became unclear to someone, and this is a mubham (obscure) door, that is, a closed path. Then this name was specialized to every four-footed creature on land and sea. The al-anʿam (grazing livestock) are the camels, cattle and sheep. The Exalted said: ﴿And the cattle—He created them for you; in them is warmth﴾ [al-Nahl: 5], up to His saying: ﴿And the horses, the mules and the donkeys﴾ [al-Nahl: 8]. So the Exalted distinguished between the cattle and the horses, mules and donkeys. And He said: ﴿Among what Our hands have made, cattle, of which they are owners﴾ ﴿And We subjected them to them, so some of them they ride and some of them they eat﴾ [Ya Sin: 72]. And He said: ﴿And of the cattle are beasts of burden and those for carpeting; eat of what Allah has provided for you﴾ [al-An'am: 142]

up to His saying: ﴿eight pairs: two of the sheep and two of the goats﴾ [al-An'am: 143], and up to His saying: ﴿and of camels two and of cattle two﴾ [al-An'am: 144]. Al-Wahidi, may Allah have mercy on him, said: the hoofed animals are not included in the name al-anʿam, because it is derived from the softness of the tread.

Having known this, we say: there are questions regarding the wording of the verse:

The first: bahimah is a generic noun (ism al-jins), and al-anʿam is a specific noun (ism al-nawʿ), so His saying: ﴿beast of the grazing livestock﴾ runs like the saying of one who says: "animal of the human," and it is superfluous.

The second: if He had said: "Lawful for you are the al-anʿam," the speech would have been complete, as is evident from His saying in another verse: ﴿And lawful for you are the grazing livestock, except what is recited to you﴾. So what is the benefit in adding the word bahimah in this verse?

The third: He mentioned the word bahimah in the singular, and the word al-anʿam in the plural. What is the benefit of this?

The answer to the first question is in two respects:

The first: the intended meaning of bahimah and of al-anʿam is one thing, and the idafah (annexation) of bahimah to al-anʿam is for clarification, and this annexation is in the sense of "min" (of), like "a ring of silver," meaning the beast from among the grazing livestock; or for emphasis, like our saying: "the very self of the thing, its essence, and its very eye."

The second: the intended meaning of bahimah is one thing, and the intended meaning of al-anʿam is another thing. On this supposition there are two views:

The first: the intended meaning of "beast of the grazing livestock" is gazelles, the wild cattle and the like, as though they meant what resembles the grazing livestock and approaches them among the kinds of beasts in chewing the cud and lacking fangs, so it was annexed to al-anʿam because of the resemblance.

The second: the intended meaning of "beast of the grazing livestock" is the fetuses of the grazing livestock. It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a cow was slaughtered and a fetus was found in its belly, so Ibn ʿAbbas took hold of its tail and said: "This is from the beast of the grazing livestock." And from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they are the fetuses of the grazing livestock, and its slaughter is the slaughter of its mother.

Know that this view indicates the soundness of the school of al-Shafiʿi, may Allah have mercy on him, that the fetus is made lawful by the slaughter of its mother.

The second issue: The Thanawiyyah (Dualists) said: slaughtering animals is causing pain, pain is ugly, and the ugly is not approved by the Compassionate, Wise God, so it is impossible that slaughter should be lawful and permitted by the ruling of God. They said: what confirms this is that these animals have no power to defend themselves, nor do they have a tongue to argue against one who intends to cause them pain, and causing pain is ugly, except that causing pain to one who has reached this degree of helplessness and bewilderment is uglier.

Know that the sects of the Muslims divided into many sects because of this doubt. The Mukarramiyyah said: we do not grant that these animals feel pain at slaughter, rather perhaps Allah, the Exalted, removes the pain of slaughter from them. This is like obstinacy against the self-evident matters. The Mu'tazilah said: we do not grant that causing pain is ugly absolutely; rather it is ugly only when it is not preceded by a crime and not accompanied by a recompense, and here Allah, glorified is He, compensates these animals in the Hereafter with noble recompenses, and then this slaughter ceases to be injustice. They said: what indicates the soundness of what we have said is what is established in the intellects, that it is good to bear the pain of phlebotomy and cupping for the sake of seeking health; so when bearing a small pain is good for the sake of a great benefit, the same applies to slaughter. Our companions said: the permission to slaughter animals is a disposition by Allah, the Exalted, in His dominion, and the owner has no objection raised against him when he disposes of his own property. The matter is long and is mentioned in the science of the principles (uṣūl), and Allah knows best.

The third issue: Some of them said: His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock﴾ is mujmal (ambiguous), because permissibility (ihlal) is attributed to actions, and here it is attributed to the essences, so its application to its apparent meaning is impossible, and there must be an implied verb; and implying one of the actions is not preferable to another. So it is possible that the intended meaning is the permission to benefit from its hide, its bones, its wool or its flesh, or the intended meaning is the permission to benefit by eating. There is no doubt that the wording admits all of these, so the verse becomes ambiguous. However, His saying: ﴿And the cattle—He created them for you; in them is warmth and benefits, and from them you eat﴾ [al-Nahl: 5] indicates that the intended meaning of His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock﴾ is the permission to benefit from them in all these respects.

* *

Know that when the Exalted mentioned His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock﴾, He attached to it two kinds of exception:

The first: His saying: ﴿except what is recited to you﴾. Know that the apparent meaning of this exception is mujmal, and the exception of an ambiguous statement from a detailed statement makes what remains after the exception also ambiguous. However, the exegetes have unanimously agreed that the intended meaning of this exception is what is mentioned after this verse, which is His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked, the strangled, the beaten to death, the fallen to death, the gored, and what a predator has eaten, except what you have slaughtered, and what is sacrificed on stone altars﴾. The reasoning is that His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the animals of grazing livestock﴾ requires their permissibility for them in all respects, so Allah, the Exalted, clarified that if they were carrion, or beaten to death, or fallen to death, or gored, or seized by a predator, or slaughtered not in the name of Allah, the Exalted, then they are prohibited.

The second kind of exception: His saying: ﴿other than those who hunt game while you are in the state of ihram﴾. There are several issues concerning it:

The first issue: When He made the beast of the grazing livestock lawful, He mentioned the distinction between its game and its non-game, so we know that whatever of it is game is lawful when not in the state of ihram, but not when in ihram; and whatever is not game is lawful in both states altogether, and Allah knows best.

The second issue: His saying: ﴿while you are in the state of ihram﴾ means: muhrimun, that is, entering into ihram for the hajj or the ʿumrah or one of them. One says: "He entered ihram for the hajj and ʿumrah, so he is muhrim and ḥurum," just as one says: "He became junub (in major impurity), so he is mujnib and junub." The word is the same for the singular and the plural; one says "qawm ḥurum" just as one says "qawm junub." The Exalted said: ﴿And if you are junub, then purify yourselves﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6].

Know that when we say "aḥrama al-rajul" (the man entered ihram), it has two meanings: the first is this.

The second: that he entered the Haram. So His saying: ﴿while you are in the state of ihram﴾ encompasses both meanings, and hunting is forbidden to one who is in the Haram just as it is forbidden to one who is in ihram for the hajj or ʿumrah; this is the view of the jurists.

Third issue: Know that the apparent meaning of the verse requires that hunting is forbidden to the one in ihram (the state of pilgrim sanctity). A parallel to this verse is His, exalted is He, saying: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾. Here "idha" (when) is a conditional particle, and what is made dependent on a conditional word is non-existent when that condition is absent. However, He, exalted is He, clarified in another verse that what is forbidden to the one in ihram is only land game, not sea game. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Lawful for you is the game of the sea and its food, as a provision for you and for the travelers; but forbidden to you is the game of the land as long as you are in the state of ihram﴾ [al-Ma'idah 5:96]. Thus this verse became an explanation of those unrestricted verses.

Fourth issue: The word "ghayr" (not, without) is in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of His saying: ﴿you were made lawful﴾, just as you say: "The food was made lawful for you, without transgressing in it." Al-Farra' said: It is like your saying: "Such-and-such a thing was made lawful for you, not wasteful of it and not exceeding bounds." The meaning is: the beast of cattle was made lawful for you, except that you hunt game while in the state of ihram, for that is not lawful for you while you are in ihram.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Indeed, Allah decrees what He wills﴾. The meaning is that He, exalted is He, permitted cattle in all circumstances, and permitted hunting in some circumstances but not others. If someone asks: what is the reason for this detailed distinction and specification, the answer is that He, exalted is He, is the Owner and Creator of things, so there is no objection to His ruling in any way whatsoever. This is what our companions (the Ash'aris) say: the cause of the goodness of imposing obligations is lordship and servanthood, not what the Mu'tazilah say about safeguarding of interests.

قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ ولا الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ ولا الهَدْيَ ولا القَلائِدَ ولا آمِّينَ البَيْتَ الحَرامَ﴾ .

اعْلَمْ أنَّهُ تَعالى: لَمّا حَرَّمَ الصَّيْدَ عَلى المُحْرِمِ في الآيَةِ الأُولى أكَّدَ ذَلِكَ بِالنَّهْيِ في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ عَنْ مُخالَفَةِ تَكالِيفِ اللَّهِ تَعالى فَقالَ: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ﴾ .

واعْلَمْ أنَّ الشَّعائِرَ جَمْعٌ، والأكْثَرُونَ عَلى أنَّها جَمْعُ شَعِيرَةٍ. وقالَ ابْنُ فارِسٍ: واحِدُها شَعارَةٌ، والشَّعِيرَةُ فَعِيلَةٌ بِمَعْنى مُفَعَّلَةٍ، والمُشَّعَرَةُ المُعَلَّمَةُ، والأشْعارُ الأعْلامُ، وكُلُّ شَيْءٍ أُشْعِرَ فَقَدْ أُعْلِمَ، وكُلُّ شَيْءٍ جُعِلَ عَلَمًا عَلى شَيْءٍ أوْ عُلِّمَ بِعَلامَةٍ جازَ أنْ يُسَمّى شَعِيرَةً، فالهَدْيُ الَّذِي يُهْدى إلى مَكَّةَ يُسَمّى شَعائِرَ لِأنَّها مُعَلَّمَةٌ بِعَلاماتٍ دالَّةٍ عَلى كَوْنِها هَدْيًا. واخْتَلَفَ المُفَسِّرُونَ (عِلْمُ التَّفْسِيرِ: شَرْحُ مَعاني القُرْآنِ) في المُرادِ بِشَعائِرِ اللَّهِ، وفِيهِ قَوْلانِ:

الأوَّلُ: قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ﴾ أيْ: لا تُخِلُّوا بِشَيْءٍ مِن شَعائِرِ اللَّهِ وفَرائِضِهِ الَّتِي حَدَّها لِعِبادِهِ وأوْجَبَها عَلَيْهِمْ، وعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ فَشَعائِرُ اللَّهِ عامٌّ في جَمِيعِ تَكالِيفِهِ غَيْرُ مَخْصُوصٍ بِشَيْءٍ مُعَيَّنٍ، ويَقْرُبُ مِنهُ قَوْلُ الحَسَنِ: شَعائِرُ اللَّهِ دِينُ اللَّهِ.

والثّانِي: أنَّ المُرادَ مِنهُ شَيْءٌ خاصٌّ مِنَ التَّكالِيفِ، وعَلى هَذا القَوْلِ فَذَكَرُوا وُجُوهًا:

الأوَّلُ: المُرادُ لا تَحِلُّوا ما حَرَّمَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْكم في حالِ إحْرامِكم مِنَ الصَّيْدِ.

والثّانِي: قالَ ابْنُ عَبّاسٍ: إنَّ المُشْرِكِينَ كانُوا يَحُجُّونَ البَيْتَ ويُهْدُونَ الهَدايا ويُعَظِّمُونَ المَشاعِرَ ويَنْحَرُونَ، فَأرادَ المُسْلِمُونَ أنْ يُغِيرُوا عَلَيْهِمْ، فَأنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى: ﴿لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ﴾ .

الثّالِثُ: قالَ الفَرّاءُ: كانَتْ عامَّةُ العَرَبِ لا يَرَوْنَ الصَّفا والمَرْوَةَ مِن شَعائِرِ الحَجِّ ولا يَطُوفُونَ بِهِما، فَأنْزَلَ اللَّهُ تَعالى: لا تَسْتَحِلُّوا تَرْكَ شَيْءٍ مِن مَناسِكِ الحَجِّ وأْتُوا بِجَمِيعِها عَلى سَبِيلِ الكَمالِ والتَّمامِ.

الرّابِعُ: قالَ بَعْضُهم: الشَّعائِرُ هي الهَدايا تُطْعَنُ في أسَنامِها وتُقَلَّدُ لِيُعْلَمَ أنَّها هَدْيٌ، وهو قَوْلُ أبِي عُبَيْدَةَ، قالَ: ويَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿والبُدْنَ جَعَلْناها لَكم مِن شَعائِرِ اللَّهِ﴾ [الحَجِّ: ٣٦] وهَذا عِنْدِي ضَعِيفٌ لِأنَّهُ تَعالى ذَكَرَ شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ عَطَفَ عَلَيْها الهَدْيَ، والمَعْطُوفُ يَجِبُ أنْ يَكُونَ مُغايِرًا لِلْمَعْطُوفِ عَلَيْهِ.

ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿ولا الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ﴾ أيْ: لا تُحِلُّوا الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ بِالقِتالِ فِيهِ.

واعْلَمْ أنَّ الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ هو الشَّهْرُ الَّذِي كانَتِ العَرَبُ تُعَظِّمُهُ وتُحَرِّمُ القِتالَ فِيهِ، قالَ تَعالى: ﴿إنَّ عِدَّةَ الشُّهُورِ عِنْدَ اللَّهِ اثْنا عَشَرَ شَهْرًا في كِتابِ اللَّهِ يَوْمَ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ والأرْضَ مِنها أرْبَعَةٌ حُرُمٌ﴾ [التَّوْبَةِ: ٣٦] فَقِيلَ: هي ذُو القَعْدَةِ وذُو الحِجَّةِ والمُحَرَّمُ ورَجَبٌ، فَقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ولا الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ﴾ يَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ إشارَةً إلى

[صفحة ١٠٢]

جَمِيعِ هَذِهِ الأشْهُرِ كَما يُطْلَقُ اسْمُ الواحِدِ عَلى الجِنْسِ، ويَجُوزُ أنْ يَكُونَ المُرادُ هو رَجَبٌ لِأنَّهُ أكْمَلُ الأشْهُرِ الأرْبَعَةِ في هَذِهِ الصِّفَةِ.

* * *
ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿ولا الهَدْيَ﴾ قالَ الواحِدِيُّ (أبُو الحَسَنِ الواحِدِيُّ، مُفَسِّرٌ): الهَدْيُ ما أُهْدِيَ إلى بَيْتِ اللَّهِ مِن ناقَةٍ أوْ بَقَرَةٍ أوْ شاةٍ، واحِدُها هَدْيَةٌ بِتَسْكِينِ الدّالِ، ويُقالُ أيْضًا هَدِيَّةٌ، وجَمْعُها هَدِيٌّ. قالَ الشّاعِرُ:

حَلَفْتُ بِرَبِّ مَكَّةَ والمُصَلّى وأعْناقِ الهَدِيِّ مُقَلَّداتٍ

ونَظِيرُ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ قَوْلُهُ تَعالى: ﴿هَدْيًا بالِغَ الكَعْبَةِ﴾ [المائِدَةِ: ٩٥] وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿والهَدْيَ مَعْكُوفًا أنْ يَبْلُغَ مَحِلَّهُ﴾ [الفَتْحِ: ٢٥] .

* * *
ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿ولا القَلائِدَ﴾ والقَلائِدُ جَمْعُ قِلادَةٍ وهي الَّتِي تُشَدُّ عَلى عُنُقِ البَعِيرِ وغَيْرِهِ وهي مَشْهُورَةٌ. وفي التَّفْسِيرِ وُجُوهٌ:

الأوَّلُ: المُرادُ مِنهُ الهَدْيُ ذَواتُ القَلائِدِ، وعُطِفَتْ عَلى الهَدْيِ مُبالَغَةً في التَّوْصِيَةِ بِها لِأنَّها أشْرَفُ الهَدْيِ كَقَوْلِهِ ﴿وجِبْرِيلَ ومِيكالَ﴾ [البَقَرَةِ: ٩٨] كَأنَّهُ قِيلَ: والقَلائِدُ مِنها خُصُوصًا.

الثّانِي: أنَّهُ نَهى عَنِ التَّعَرُّضِ لِقَلائِدِ الهَدْيِ مُبالَغَةً في النَّهْيِ عَنِ التَّعَرُّضِ لِلْهَدْيِ عَلى مَعْنى: ولا تُحِلُّوا قَلائِدَها فَضْلًا عَنْ أنْ تُحِلُّوها، كَما قالَ ﴿ولا يُبْدِينَ زِينَتَهُنَّ﴾ [النُّورِ: ٣١] فَنَهى عَنْ إبْداءِ الزِّينَةِ مُبالَغَةً في النَّهْيِ عَنْ إبْداءِ مَواضِعِها.

الثّالِثُ: قالَ بَعْضُهم: كانَتِ العَرَبُ في الجاهِلِيَّةِ مُواظِبِينَ عَلى المُحارَبَةِ إلّا في الأشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ، فَمَن وُجِدَ في غَيْرِ هَذِهِ الأشْهُرِ الحُرُمِ أُصِيبَ مِنهُ، إلّا أنْ يَكُونَ مُشْعِرًا بَدَنَةً أوْ بَقَرَةً مِن لِحاءِ شَجَرِ الحَرَمِ، أوْ مُحْرِمًا بِعُمْرَةٍ إلى البَيْتِ، فَحِينَئِذٍ لا يُتَعَرَّضُ لَهُ، فَأمَرَ اللَّهُ المُسْلِمِينَ بِتَقْرِيرِ هَذا المَعْنى.

* * *
ثُمَّ قالَ: ﴿ولا آمِّينَ البَيْتَ الحَرامَ﴾ أيْ: قَوْمًا قاصِدِينَ المَسْجِدَ الحَرامَ، وقَرَأ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ: (ولا آمِّي البَيْتِ الحَرامِ) عَلى الإضافَةِ.

* *
* * *
ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِن رَبِّهِمْ ورِضْوانًا﴾ وفِيهِ مَسائِلُ:

المَسْألَةُ الأُولى: قَرَأ حُمَيْدُ بْنُ قَيْسٍ الأعْرَجُ (تَبْتَغُونَ) بِالتّاءِ عَلى خِطابِ المُؤْمِنِينَ.

المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: في تَفْسِيرِ الفَضْلِ والرِّضْوانِ وجْهانِ:

الأوَّلُ: يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِن رَبِّهِمْ بِالتِّجارَةِ المُباحَةِ لَهم في حَجِّهِمْ، كَقَوْلِهِ ﴿لَيْسَ عَلَيْكم جُناحٌ أنْ تَبْتَغُوا فَضْلًا مِن رَبِّكُمْ﴾ [البَقَرَةِ: ١٩٨] قالُوا: نَزَلَتْ في تِجاراتِهِمْ أيّامَ المَوْسِمِ، والمَعْنى: لا تَمْنَعُوهم فَإنَّما قَصَدُوا البَيْتَ لِإصْلاحِ مَعاشِهِمْ ومَعادِهِمْ، فابْتِغاءُ الفَضْلِ لِلدُّنْيا، وابْتِغاءُ الرِّضْوانِ لِلْآخِرَةِ. قالَ أهْلُ العِلْمِ: إنَّ المُشْرِكِينَ كانُوا يَقْصِدُونَ بِحَجِّهِمُ ابْتِغاءَ رِضْوانِ اللَّهِ وإنْ كانُوا لا يَنالُونَ ذَلِكَ، فَلا يَبْعُدُ أنْ يَحْصُلَ لَهم بِسَبَبِ هَذا القَصْدِ نَوْعٌ مِنَ الحُرْمَةِ.

[صفحة ١٠٣]

والوَجْهُ الثّانِي: أنَّ المُرادَ بِفَضْلِ اللَّهِ الثَّوابُ، وبِالرِّضْوانِ أنْ يَرْضى عَنْهم، وذَلِكَ لِأنَّ الكافِرَ وإنْ كانَ لا يَنالُ الفَضْلَ والرِّضْوانَ لَكِنَّهُ يَظُنُّ أنَّهُ بِفِعْلِهِ طالِبٌ لَهُما، فَيَجُوزُ أنْ يُوصَفَ بِذَلِكَ بِناءً عَلى ظَنِّهِ، قالَ تَعالى: ﴿وانْظُرْ إلى إلَهِكَ﴾ [طه: ٩٧] وقالَ: ﴿ذُقْ إنَّكَ أنْتَ العَزِيزُ الكَرِيمُ﴾ [الدُّخانِ: ٤٩] .

المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: اخْتَلَفَ النّاسُ فَقالَ بَعْضُهم: هَذِهِ الآيَةُ مَنسُوخَةٌ (النَّسْخُ: إبْطالُ حُكْمٍ شَرْعِيٍّ بِدَلِيلٍ لاحِقٍ)، لِأنَّ قَوْلَهُ: ﴿لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ ولا الشَّهْرَ الحَرامَ﴾ يَقْتَضِي حُرْمَةَ القِتالِ في الشَّهْرِ الحَرامِ، وذَلِكَ مَنسُوخٌ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فاقْتُلُوا المُشْرِكِينَ حَيْثُ وجَدْتُمُوهُمْ﴾ [التَّوْبَةِ: ٥] وقَوْلُهُ: ﴿ولا آمِّينَ البَيْتَ الحَرامَ﴾ يَقْتَضِي حُرْمَةَ مَنعِ المُشْرِكِينَ عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ وذَلِكَ مَنسُوخٌ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَلا يَقْرَبُوا المَسْجِدَ الحَرامَ بَعْدَ عامِهِمْ هَذا﴾ [التَّوْبَةِ: ٢٨] وهَذا قَوْلُ كَثِيرٍ مِنَ المُفَسِّرِينَ كابْنِ عَبّاسٍ ومُجاهِدٍ والحَسَنِ وقَتادَةَ. وقالَ الشَّعْبِيُّ: لَمْ يُنْسَخْ مِن سُورَةِ المائِدَةِ إلّا هَذِهِ الآيَةُ. وقالَ قَوْمٌ آخَرُونَ مِنَ المُفَسِّرِينَ: هَذِهِ الآيَةُ غَيْرُ مَنسُوخَةٍ، وهَؤُلاءِ لَهم طَرِيقانِ:

الأوَّلُ: أنَّ اللَّهَ تَعالى أمَرَنا في هَذِهِ الآيَةِ أنْ لا نُخِيفَ مَن يَقْصِدُ بَيْتَهُ مِنَ المُسْلِمِينَ، وحَرَّمَ عَلَيْنا أخْذَ الهَدْيِ مِنَ المُهْدِينَ إذا كانُوا مُسْلِمِينَ، والدَّلِيلُ عَلَيْهِ أوَّلُ الآيَةِ وآخِرُها، أمّا أوَّلُ الآيَةِ فَهو قَوْلُهُ: ﴿لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ﴾ وشَعائِرُ اللَّهِ إنَّما تَلِيقُ بِنُسُكِ المُسْلِمِينَ وطاعاتِهِمْ لا بِنُسُكِ الكُفّارِ، وأمّا آخِرُ الآيَةِ فَهو قَوْلُهُ: ﴿يَبْتَغُونَ فَضْلًا مِن رَبِّهِمْ ورِضْوانًا﴾ وهَذا إنَّما يَلِيقُ بِالمُسْلِمِ لا بِالكافِرِ.

الثّانِي: قالَ أبُو مُسْلِمٍ الأصْفَهانِيُّ: المُرادُ بِالآيَةِ الكُفّارُ الَّذِينَ كانُوا في عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ، فَلَمّا زالَ العَهْدُ بِسُورَةِ بَراءَةٌ زالَ ذَلِكَ الحَظْرُ ولَزِمَ المُرادُ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعالى: ﴿فَلا يَقْرَبُوا المَسْجِدَ الحَرامَ بَعْدَ عامِهِمْ هَذا﴾ . [التَّوْبَةِ: ٢٨ ] .

* * *
ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿وإذا حَلَلْتُمْ فاصْطادُوا﴾ وفِيهِ مَسائِلُ:

المَسْألَةُ الأُولى: قُرِئَ: وإذا أحْلَلْتُمْ، يُقالُ حَلَّ المُحْرِمُ وأحَلَّ، وقُرِئَ بِكَسْرِ الفاءِ (فاصْطادُوا)، وقِيلَ هو بَدَلٌ مِن كَسْرِ الهَمْزَةِ عِنْدَ الِابْتِداءِ.

المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: هَذِهِ الآيَةُ مُتَعَلِّقَةٌ بِقَوْلِهِ: ﴿غَيْرَ مُحِلِّي الصَّيْدِ وأنْتُمْ حُرُمٌ﴾ يَعْنِي لَمّا كانَ المانِعُ مِن حِلِّ الِاصْطِيادِ هو الإحْرامُ، فَإذا زالَ الإحْرامُ وجَبَ أنْ يَزُولَ المَنعُ.

المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: ظاهِرُ الأمْرِ وإنْ كانَ لِلْوُجُوبِ إلّا أنَّهُ لا يُفِيدُ هَهُنا إلّا الإباحَةَ. وكَذا في قَوْلِهِ: ﴿فَإذا قُضِيَتِ الصَّلاةُ فانْتَشِرُوا في الأرْضِ﴾ [الجُمُعَةِ: ١٠] ونَظِيرُهُ قَوْلُ القائِلِ: لا تَدْخُلَنَّ هَذِهِ الدّارَ حَتّى تُؤَدِّيَ ثَمَنَها، فَإذا أدَّيْتَ فادْخُلْها، أيْ: فَإذا أدَّيْتَ فَقَدْ أُبِيحَ لَكَ دُخُولُها، وحاصِلُ الكَلامِ أنّا إنَّما عَرَفْنا أنَّ الأمْرَ هَهُنا لَمْ يُفِدِ الوُجُوبَ بِدَلِيلٍ مُنْفَصِلٍ واللَّهُ أعْلَمُ.

* * *
ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿ولا يَجْرِمَنَّكم شَنَآنُ قَوْمٍ أنْ صَدُّوكم عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ أنْ تَعْتَدُوا وتَعاوَنُوا عَلى البِرِّ والتَّقْوى ولا تَعاوَنُوا عَلى الإثْمِ والعُدْوانِ﴾ وفي الآيَةِ مَسائِلُ:

المَسْألَةُ الأُولى: قالَ القَفّالُ (أبُو بَكْرٍ القَفّالُ، مُفَسِّرٌ) - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -: هَذا مَعْطُوفٌ عَلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿لا تُحِلُّوا شَعائِرَ اللَّهِ﴾ إلى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿ولا آمِّينَ البَيْتَ الحَرامَ﴾ يَعْنِي ولا تَحْمِلَنَّكم عَداوَتُكم لِقَوْمٍ مِن أجْلِ أنَّهم صَدُّوكم عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ عَلى أنْ تَعْتَدُوا فَتَمْنَعُوهم عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ، فَإنَّ الباطِلَ لا يَجُوزُ أنْ يُعْتَدى بِهِ. ولَيْسَ لِلنّاسِ أنْ يُعِينَ بَعْضُهم بَعْضًا عَلى العُدْوانِ حَتّى إذا تَعَدّى واحِدٌ مِنهم عَلى الآخَرِ تَعَدّى ذَلِكَ الآخَرُ عَلَيْهِ، لَكِنَّ الواجِبَ أنْ يُعِينَ بَعْضُهم بَعْضًا عَلى ما فِيهِ البِرُّ والتَّقْوى، فَهَذا هو المَقْصُودُ مِنَ الآيَةِ.

[صفحة ١٠٤]

المَسْألَةُ الثّانِيَةُ: قالَ صاحِبُ ”الكَشّافِ“ (الزَّمَخْشَرِيُّ): (جَرَمَ) يَجْرِي مَجْرى كَسَبَ في تَعَدِّيهِ تارَةً إلى مَفْعُولٍ واحِدٍ، وتارَةً إلى اثْنَيْنِ، تَقُولُ: جَرَمَ ذَنْبًا نَحْوَ كَسَبَهُ، وجَرَمْتُهُ ذَنْبًا نَحْوَ كَسَبْتُهُ إيّاهُ، ويُقالُ: أجْرَمْتُهُ ذَنْبًا عَلى نَقْلِ المُتَعَدِّي إلى مَفْعُولٍ بِالهَمْزَةِ إلى مَفْعُولَيْنِ، كَقَوْلِهِمْ: أكْسَبْتُهُ ذَنْبًا، وعَلَيْهِ قِراءَةُ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ ”ولا يُجْرِمَنَّكم“ بِضَمِّ الياءِ، وأوَّلُ المَفْعُولَيْنِ عَلى القِراءَتَيْنِ ضَمِيرُ المُخاطَبِينَ.

والثّانِي: أنْ تَعْتَدُوا، والمَعْنى لا يَكْسِبَنَّكم بُغْضُ قَوْمٍ لِأنْ صَدُّوكُمُ الِاعْتِداءَ ولا يَحْمِلَنَّكم عَلَيْهِ.

المَسْألَةُ الثّالِثَةُ: الشَّنَآنُ البُغْضُ، يُقالُ: شَنَأْتُ الرَّجُلَ أشَنْؤُهُ شَنَأً ومَشْنَأً وشِنْأةً ومَشْنَأةً وشَنَآنًا بِفَتْحِ الشِّينِ وكَسْرِها، ويُقالُ: رَجُلٌ شَنَآنٌ وامْرَأةٌ شَنَآنَةٌ مَصْرُوفانِ، ويُقالُ شَنَآنُ بِغَيْرِ صَرْفٍ، وفَعَلانُ قَدْ جاءَ وصْفًا وقَدْ جاءَ مَصْدَرًا.

المَسْألَةُ الرّابِعَةُ: قَرَأ ابْنُ عامِرٍ وأبُو بَكْرٍ عَنْ عاصِمٍ وإسْماعِيلُ عَنْ نافِعٍ بِجَزْمِ النُّونِ الأُولى، والباقُونَ بِالفَتْحِ. قالُوا: والفَتْحُ أجْوَدُ لِكَثْرَةِ نَظائِرِها في المَصادِرِ كالضَّرَبانِ والسَّيَلانِ والغَلَيانِ والغَشَيانِ، وأمّا بِالسُّكُونِ فَقَدْ جاءَ في الأكْثَرِ وصْفًا. قالَ الواحِدِيُّ: ومِمّا جاءَ مَصْدَرًا قَوْلُهم: لَوَيْتُهُ حَقَّهُ لَيّانًا، وشَنْآنٌ في قَوْلِ أبِي عُبَيْدَةَ. وأنْشَدَ لِلْأحْوَصِ:

وإنْ عابَ فِيهِ ذُو الشَّنْآنِ وفَنَّدا

فَقَوْلُهُ: ذُو الشَّنْآنِ عَلى التَّخْفِيفِ كَقَوْلِهِمْ: إنِّي ظَمْآنٌ، وفُلانٌ ظَمْآنٌ، بِحَذْفِ الهَمْزَةِ وإلْقاءِ حَرَكَتِها عَلى ما قَبْلَها.

المَسْألَةُ الخامِسَةُ: قَرَأ ابْنُ كَثِيرٍ وأبُو عَمْرٍو (وإنْ صَدُّوكم) بِكَسْرِ الألِفِ عَلى الشَّرْطِ والجَزاءِ، والباقُونَ بِفَتْحِ الألِفِ، يَعْنِي لِأنْ صَدُّوكم. قالَ مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ جَرِيرٍ الطَّبَرِيُّ: وهَذِهِ القِراءَةُ هي الِاخْتِيارُ لِأنَّ مَعْنى صَدِّهِمْ إيّاهم عَنِ المَسْجِدِ الحَرامِ مَنعُ أهْلِ مَكَّةَ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ والمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ الحُدَيْبِيَةِ عَنِ العُمْرَةِ، وهَذِهِ السُّورَةُ نَزَلَتْ بَعْدَ الحُدَيْبِيَةِ، وكانَ هَذا الصَّدُّ مُتَقَدِّمًا لا مَحالَةَ عَلى نُزُولِ هَذِهِ الآيَةِ.

* * *
ثُمَّ قالَ تَعالى: ﴿واتَّقُوا اللَّهَ إنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ العِقابِ﴾ والمُرادُ مِنهُ التَّهْدِيدُ والوَعِيدُ، يَعْنِي اتَّقُوا اللَّهَ ولا تَسْتَحِلُّوا شَيْئًا مِن مَحارِمِهِ إنَّ اللَّهَ شَدِيدُ العِقابِ، لا يَطِيقُ أحَدٌ عِقابَهُ.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 5, verse 3 (part 1 of 3):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Forbidden to you are carrion, blood, the flesh of swine, that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked, the strangled animal, the animal beaten to death, the animal that falls to its death, the animal gored to death, what a wild beast has eaten, except what you slaughter, and what is sacrificed on stone altars, and that you seek decision through divining arrows.﴾

Know that He, the Exalted, said at the beginning of the surah: ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle﴾, and then He mentioned exceptions to this that are recited to you. Here Allah the Exalted mentions those forms excepted from that general rule, and they are eleven types:

The first: carrion (al-maytah). The people used to say: "You eat what you kill, but you do not eat what Allah kills."

Know that the prohibition of carrion accords with what is found in reason, because blood is an extremely subtle substance. When an animal dies of its own accord, the blood remains confined in its veins, rots, spoils, and great harms result from eating it.

The second: blood. The author of al-Kashshaf said: They used to fill the intestines with blood, roast them, and feed them to the guest, so Allah the Exalted forbade this to them.

The third: the flesh of swine. The people of knowledge said: Food becomes part of the substance of the one who eats it, so there must necessarily arise in the eater qualities and characteristics of the same kind as those present in the food. The swine is naturally disposed to great greed and intense desire for appetites, so its flesh was forbidden to man, lest he take on that condition. As for the sheep, it is an animal in the utmost state of tranquillity, as if it were a being devoid of all dispositions, so no foreign condition alien to human states arises in a person from eating its flesh.

The fourth: that over which the name of other than Allah has been invoked. The ihlal (invocation) is raising the voice. From it one says "Fulan invoked (ahalla) for the Hajj" when he recited the talbiyah with it, and from it "the child cried out (istahalla)", meaning his crying when born. They used to say at the slaughter: "In the name of al-Lat and al-Uzza", so Allah the Exalted forbade that.

The fifth: the strangled animal (al-munkhaniqah). One says: he strangled him, so he was strangled (ikhtanaqa). Al-khanq and al-ikhtinaq mean the constriction of the throat.

Know that the strangled animal takes several forms. Among them: the people of the Jahiliyyah used to strangle a sheep, and when it died they ate it. Among them: that which is strangled by the hunter's rope. Among them: that whose head is inserted between two sticks in a tree, so it chokes and dies. In sum, in whatever manner it was strangled, it is forbidden.

Know that this strangled animal is of the same kind as carrion, because when it died without its blood flowing, it was like one who died of its own accord.

The sixth: the beaten animal (al-mawqudhah), which is one beaten until it dies. One says: waqadhahu and awqadhahu when he beat it until it died. The beaten animal includes what is struck by a pellet bow and dies. It is also in the sense of carrion and in the sense of the strangled animal, for it died without its blood flowing.

The seventh: the animal that falls to its death (al-mutaraddiyah). The mutaraddi is one who falls into ruin (radaa), which is destruction. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nor will his wealth avail him when he falls (tarradda)﴾ [al-Layl: 11], meaning he fell into the Fire. One says: Fulan fell (tarradda) from the roof. So the mutaraddiyah is the animal that falls from a mountain or an elevated place and dies. This too is of the kind of carrion, because it died and blood did not flow from it. It includes also the case where an arrow strikes it while it is on the mountain and it falls to the ground; its eating is forbidden, because it is not known whether it died by the fall or by the arrow.

The eighth: the gored animal (al-nateehah), which is one gored until it dies. This is like two sheep that butt each other until both die or one of them dies. This too falls under carrion, because it died without the flowing of blood.

Know that the entry of the ta' marbuta into these four words, namely al-munkhaniqah, al-mawqudhah, al-mutaraddiyah, and al-nateehah, is only because they are qualifiers of a feminine noun which is the sheep, as if it were said: "Forbidden to you is the sheep that is strangled, beaten, fallen, and gored." The sheep was singled out because it is among the most common of what people eat, and speech follows the general and the predominant, while the intended meaning is the whole.

If it is said: Why was the ta' affixed to al-nateehah, though originally it was a manṭūḥah, and in such a position the ta' is elided, as in the expressions kaffun khadeeb (a hand dyed), lihyatun duhayn (a beard oiled), 'aynun kahil (an eye darkened)?

We say: The ta' is elided from the fa'eelah only when it is a qualifier of a noun preceding it. When the noun is not mentioned and the qualifier is mentioned, you place it in the position of the noun, saying: "I saw the slain (qatilah) of the sons of Fulan" with the ta', because if you do not add the ta', it is not known whether he is a man or a woman. Accordingly, the ta' entered al-nateehah because it is a qualifier of an unmentioned feminine noun, which is the sheep.

* * *

The ninth: His saying: ﴿what a wild beast has eaten, except what you slaughter﴾. In this are several issues:

First issue: al-sabu' (wild beast) is a name applied to whatever has fangs and attacks humans and animals and preys upon them, like the lion and what is below it. It is permissible to lighten it, so one says sab' and sab'ah. In a report from Abu 'Amr: al-sab' with a sukun on the ba'. And Ibn 'Abbas recited: wa-akeelu al-sab'i (and what the beast has eaten).

Second issue: Qatadah said: When a beast wounded something and killed it and ate part of it, the people of the Jahiliyyah would eat what remained, so Allah the Exalted forbade it. In the verse there is an elided element, its estimated meaning being: "and what the beast has eaten of it," because what the beast has eaten is consumed and has no ruling, and the ruling pertains only to what remains.

Third issue: The root meaning of dhakah in the language is the completion of a thing. From it comes dhaka in understanding, which is its completion; from it dhaka in age; and it was said: the running of the mudhakkiyat is ghilab, meaning the running of the aged mares who have reached maturity. The interpretation of the completion of age is the peak of youth; if it falls short of that or exceeds it, it is not called dhaka in age. One says: dhakkaytu al-nar, meaning I completed its kindling.

Having known this root, we say: The exception mentioned in His saying ﴿except what you slaughter﴾ has several opinions:

The first: that it is an exception from everything preceding from His saying ﴿and the strangled﴾ up to His saying ﴿and what the beast has eaten﴾. This is the view of 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, and Qatadah. According to this, if you reach its slaughter, by finding that it has an eye that blinks, or a tail that moves, or a leg that kicks, then slaughter it and it is lawful; for were it not that life remained in it, these states would not have occurred, and when you find them with these states it shows that life in its completeness is present in it.

The second opinion: that this exception is specific to His saying ﴿what the beast has eaten﴾.

The third opinion: that it is a disjunctive exception, as if it were said: "But what you slaughter of other than this is lawful."

The fourth opinion: that it is an exception from the prohibition, not from the forbidden things, meaning: "He forbade you what has passed, except what you slaughter, for it is lawful to you." According to this estimation too the exception is disjunctive.

* * *

The tenth of the forbidden things mentioned in this verse is His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and what is sacrificed on stone altars﴾, and in this are two issues:

First issue: al-nusub may be either a plural or a singular. If we say it is a plural, then its singular has three possibilities:

The first: its singular is nisab, so our saying nisab and nusub is like our saying himar and humur.

The second: its singular is al-nasb, so nasb and nusub is like saqf and suqf, rahn and ruhun, and this is the view of Ibn al-Anbari.

The third: its singular is al-nasbah. Al-Layth said: al-nusub is the plural of al-nasbah, which is a sign set up for a people. As for if we say that al-nusub is singular, its plural is ansab, so our saying nusub and ansab is like our saying tunub and atnab. Al-Azhari said: al-A'sha has made al-nusub singular, saying:

"Nor the set-up nusub, do not make it your worship, but for the sake of the outcome worship Allah your Lord."

Second issue: Some people said: the nusub are the idols. This is far-fetched, because this is conjoined to His saying ﴿what has been invoked with other than Allah﴾, and that is slaughtering in the name of idols, and the conjoined must be different from that to which it is conjoined.

Ibn Jurayj said: The nusub are not idols, for idols are carved and engraved stones, whereas these nusub are stones that they set up around the Ka'bah, and they used to slaughter before them for the idols, and they would smear them with that blood and place the flesh upon them. The Muslims said: "O Messenger of Allah, the people of the Jahiliyyah used to honor the House with blood, so we are more deserving to honor it," and the Prophet ﷺ did not reject it, so Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿Their flesh and their blood will never reach Allah﴾ [al-Hajj: 37].

Know that "ma" in His saying ﴿and what is sacrificed﴾ is in the nominative position, because it is conjoined to His saying ﴿Forbidden to you is carrion﴾ up to His saying ﴿and what the beast has eaten﴾.

Know that His saying ﴿and what is sacrificed on stone altars﴾ has two meanings:

One: and what is sacrificed under the belief in honoring the nusub.

The second: and what is sacrificed for the nusub. The lam and 'ala are interchangeable, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Peace be upon you from the companions of the right﴾ [al-Waqi'ah: 91], meaning "peace be upon you from them," and He said: ﴿And if you do evil, it is for it﴾ [al-Isra': 7], meaning "upon it."

* * *

The eleventh type: His saying, the Exalted: ﴿and that you seek decision through the divining arrows﴾. Al-Qaffal, may Allah have mercy on him, said: This was mentioned among the matters of food because it is among what the people of the Jahiliyyah innovated, and it was consistent with what they did regarding food; for slaughter upon the nusub used to take place near the House, and likewise seeking decision through the arrows, which they would perform near the House when they were there. In this are two issues:

First issue: In the verse there are two sayings:

The first: When one of them wished to travel, or to raid, or to trade, or to marry, or for another of the great affairs, he would cast the arrows. They had written on some of them: "My Lord commanded me," on some: "My Lord forbade me," and left some blank without writing. If the command came out, he proceeded with the action; if the prohibition came out, he refrained; and if the blank one came out, he repeated the procedure once more. So the meaning of seeking decision through the arrows is seeking knowledge of good and evil by means of casting the arrows.

The second: Al-Mu'arrij and many of the lexicographers said: seeking decision here is the forbidden gambling (maysir), and the arrows are the gambling arrows. The first saying is the choice of the majority.

Second issue: al-azlam are the arrows, singular zalam, as reported by al-Akhfash. The arrows were called azlam because they were zullima, meaning made smooth. One says: a man is muzallam and a woman is muzallamah when he is light and has few attachments; one says a qadah is muzallam and zalam when it is finely shaped and its form and craft are well made; and how well his arrow was zullima, meaning he made it smooth. The shanks of cattle are also called azlam, being likened to arrows for their slenderness.

* * *

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿That is a transgression (fisq)﴾, and in this there are two views:

First: that it refers to seeking decision through the arrows alone and is restricted to it.

Second: that it refers to all that has been mentioned of the permitting and forbidding, so whoever opposes it, rejecting Allah the Exalted, has disbelieved.

If it is said: According to the first view, why has seeking decision through the arrows become a transgression? Was it not that "he ﷺ loved good omen (fa'l)," and this too is among the good omen? So why has it become a transgression?

We say: al-Wahidi said: It is forbidden only because it is a seeking of knowledge of the unseen, and that is forbidden, by His saying: ﴿And no soul knows what it will earn tomorrow﴾ [Luqman: 34], and He said: ﴿Say: None in the heavens and the earth knows the unseen except Allah﴾ [al-Naml: 65]. And Abu al-Darda' narrated from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "Whoever practices soothsaying (takahhana), or seeks decision (istaqsama), or is turned from his purpose by an omen that turns him back from his journey, will not look upon the high degrees of Paradise on the Day of Resurrection."

And one may say: If seeking a conjecture based on commonly known signs were seeking knowledge of the unseen, it would follow that the knowledge of

...by divination (al-ta'bir) being either unseen knowledge or disbelief, because it is a seeking of the unseen. It would follow that relying on omens (al-fa'l) is disbelief, because it is a seeking of the unseen. It would also follow that the people of extraordinary gifts (karamat) who claim inspirations (ilhamat) are unbelievers. It is known that all of this is false. Moreover, the verses were revealed concerning knowledge, and as for one who seeks decision by the arrows, we concede that he gains no knowledge from it, but gains only a weak conjecture. Therefore that practice does not fall under these verses.

Another group said: they used to carry those arrows beside the idols, and they believed that whatever command or prohibition came out of those arrows was by the guidance and help of the idols. For this reason it was impiety (fisq) and disbelief (kufr). This view, in my opinion, is the more preferable and closer to the truth.

* * *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Today those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them, but fear Me.﴾

Know that when He, exalted is He, had enumerated earlier what He had forbidden of the beasts of grazing livestock and what He had made lawful from them, He concluded the discussion of them with His saying ﴿That is depravity (fisq)﴾. The purpose of this is to warn the responsible persons against such actions. Then He urged them to adhere to what He had prescribed for them in the most perfect manner, and so He said: ﴿Today those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion, so do not fear them﴾, meaning: do not fear the polytheists in your opposition to them concerning the laws and religions, for I have bestowed upon you the dominant state and great power, and they have become subdued and humbled before you, and they have despaired of becoming dominant over you and prevailing against you. When the matter is thus, it is incumbent upon you not to turn toward them, but to devote yourselves to obedience to God, exalted is He, and to acting upon His laws. In the verse there are several issues:

The first issue: His saying ﴿Today those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions:

The first: the intended meaning is not that very day itself, such that one might object that they had not despaired a day or two before it. Rather, it is a statement in the manner of the usage of the people of the language, meaning: there is no need for you now to flatter these disbelievers, because you have now reached a state in which none of your enemies hopes to weaken your affair. A parallel to this is his saying: "You were young yesterday, and today you have become an old man," and he does not mean by "yesterday" the day before your day, nor by "today" your present day in which you are.

The second opinion: the intended meaning is the day this verse was revealed. It was revealed on a Friday, and it was the Day of 'Arafah, after the afternoon prayer, during the Farewell Pilgrimage, in the year ten, while the Prophet ﷺ was standing at 'Arafat upon his she-camel al-'Adba'.

The second issue: His saying ﴿those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions:

The first: they despaired of your making these impurities lawful after God had made them forbidden.

The second: they despaired of overcoming you in your religion. This is because He, exalted is He, had promised to make this religion manifest over all religions, as in His saying ﴿that He may make it prevail over all religion﴾ [al-Tawbah: 33]. So He fulfilled that victory and removed fear entirely, and made the disbelievers defeated after they had been dominant, and subdued after they had been the conquerors. This second opinion is the more preferable.

The third issue: Some people said: the verse indicates that dissimulation (taqiyyah) is permissible in the face of fear. They said: because He commanded them to make these laws manifest and to act upon them openly, and He gave as the reason the removal of fear from the side of the disbelievers. This indicates that the presence of fear permits abandoning them.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you, and completed My favor upon you, and have approved Islam as a religion for you.﴾ Concerning it there are issues:

The first issue: There is a question in the verse. His saying ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾ implies that the religion was incomplete before that. That would entail that the religion to which the Prophet ﷺ was constant for most of his life was incomplete, and that he only found the complete religion in the last part of his life, for a short period.

Know that the exegetes, in order to avoid this difficulty, mentioned several answers:

The first: the intended meaning of His saying ﴿I have perfected your religion for you﴾ is the removal of fear from them and the display of power for them over their enemies. This is like when a king subdues his enemy and conquers him completely, and says: "Today our kingship has been perfected." This answer is weak, because that king's kingship before the conquest of the enemy was incomplete.

The second: the intended meaning is: I have perfected for you what you need in your obligations of learning the lawful and the unlawful. This too is weak, because if He had not perfected for them before this day what they needed of the laws, that would be a delay of the explanation beyond the time of need, and that is impermissible.

The third, which al-Qaffal mentioned and which is the chosen view: the religion was never incomplete at all, but was always complete. That is, the laws sent down from God at every time were sufficient for that time. However, God knew at the beginning of the time of the mission that what is complete on this day is not complete tomorrow and has no benefit in it. Therefore He would abrogate after establishment and would add after absence. As for the end of the period of the mission, God sent down a complete law and decreed its permanence until the Day of Resurrection. So the Law was always complete, but the first completeness was for a specific time, and the second completeness is until the Day of Resurrection. For this meaning He said: ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾.

The second issue: The opponents of analogy (qiyas) said: the verse indicates that analogy is invalid. This is because the verse shows that He has laid down a ruling for all events, for if some of them remained without a clearly stated ruling, the religion would not be complete. When the text is present for all events, then analogy, if it accords with that text, is pointless, and if it contradicts it, is invalid.

The proponents of analogy answered that the intended meaning of the perfection of the religion is that He has explained the ruling for all events, some by explicit text and some by explaining the method of knowing the ruling concerning them through analogy. For He, when He divided events into two kinds, one kind whose rulings are explicitly stated and a second kind of types in which the ruling can be derived by analogizing them to the first kind, then, when He commanded analogy and imposed it as an act of worship upon the responsible persons, that was in reality an explanation of all the rulings, and when this is so, it is a perfection of the religion.

The opponents of analogy said: the means that require attaching the non-explicit to the explicit are either decisive proofs or non-decisive proofs. If it is the first kind, there is no dispute about its validity, for we concede that analogy founded on certain premises is a valid proof. However, such an analogy has only one correct answer, and the one who opposes it deserves punishment, and a judge's ruling concerning it may be overturned, and you do not say this. If the truth is the second kind, that would be granting every person permission to rule according to what his conjecture inclines to, without knowing whether it is the religion of God or not, and whether it is the ruling that God has decreed or not. It is known that such a thing is not a perfection of the religion, but rather casting the creatures into the peril of conjectures and ignorance.

The proponents of analogy said: when the obligation of every mujtahid is to act according to what his conjecture requires, that is a perfection of the religion, and every responsible person would be certain that he is acting according to the ruling of God, and so the objection is removed.

The third issue: Our companions (the Ash'arites) said: this verse indicates the falsity of the doctrine of the Rafidah, for He, exalted is He, stated that those who disbelieved had despaired of altering the religion, and He emphasized this by His saying ﴿so do not fear them, but fear Me﴾. So if the imamate of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, had been designated by God, exalted is He, and by His Messenger ﷺ with an explicit text that was binding to obey, then whoever wished to conceal or alter it would have been in despair of that by the implication of this verse. It would then follow that none of the Companions could deny that text or alter or conceal it. But since the matter is not so, rather no mention of this text occurred, and no report or narration of it appeared, we know that the claim of this text is a lie, and that 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him, was not designated by explicit text for the imamate.

The fourth issue: The people of narrations (ahl al-athar) said: when this verse was revealed upon the Prophet ﷺ, he did not live after its revelation except eighty-one days, or eighty-two days, and no addition, abrogation, or alteration occurred in the Law after it at all. This was like the Prophet ﷺ informing of the nearness of his death, and that is an information about the unseen, and so it is a miracle. What confirms this is that when he ﷺ recited this verse to the Companions, they rejoiced greatly and showed great delight, except Abu Bakr, may God be pleased with him, who wept. When he was asked about it, he said: "This verse indicates the nearness of the death of the Messenger of God ﷺ, for after completion there is nothing but decline." So that was a proof of the perfect knowledge of al-Siddiq, in that he understood from this verse a secret that no one else grasped.

The fifth issue: Our companions said: the verse indicates that religion is not attained except by the creation and origination of God, exalted is He. The proof of this is that He attributed the perfecting of the religion to Himself, saying ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you﴾, and the perfecting of religion can come only from Him, and its origin must also be from Him.

Know that whether we say religion is an expression for action, or we say it is an expression for knowledge, or we say it is an expression for the combination of belief, verbal affirmation, and action, the inference is evident.

As for the Mu'tazilah, they interpret this as the perfecting of the explanation of the religion and the manifestation of its laws. Without doubt, what they mentioned is a departure from the literal meaning to the figurative.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and I have completed My favor upon you﴾. The meaning of "I have completed My favor upon you" by perfecting the matter of the religion and the Law is as if He said: "Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you by means of that perfecting, for there is no favor more complete than the favor of Islam."

Know that this verse also indicates that the Creator of faith is God, exalted is He. This is because we say: the religion which is Islam is a favor, and every favor is from God, so it follows that the religion of Islam is from God.

We have said that Islam is a favor for two reasons:

First: the famous expression upon the tongue of the community, which is their saying: "Praise be to God for the favor of Islam."

Second: He, exalted is He, said in this verse ﴿Today I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favor upon you﴾, mentioning the word "favor" in an indefinite form, and the apparent meaning is that the intended favor is what was previously mentioned, which is the religion.

If it is said: why is it not permissible that the intended meaning of completing the favor is making them dominant over their enemies, or that the intended meaning is making this Law such that abrogation cannot enter it?

We say: as for the first, it has already been known from His saying ﴿Today those who disbelieved have despaired of your religion﴾, so taking this verse to mean that too would be repetition.

As for the second, since the continuance of this religion is a completion of the favor, it must necessarily be that the origin of this religion is a favor. So it is established that the religion of Islam is a favor.

When this is established, we say: every favor is from God, exalted is He, and the proof for it is His saying: ﴿And whatever favor you have is from God﴾ [al-Nahl: 53]. When these two premises are established, it necessarily follows with certainty that the religion of Islam came about only by the creation of God, exalted is He, and His bringing it into existence and origination.

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and have approved Islam as a religion for you﴾. The meaning is that this is the religion that is approved by God, exalted is He. This is confirmed by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever seeks other than Islam as a religion, it will never be accepted from him﴾ [Al 'Imran: 85].

* * *

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿But whoever is compelled by severe hunger, without being inclined to sin, then indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

This is a complement to what was mentioned earlier concerning the foods that Allah the Exalted has forbidden. That is, although they are forbidden, they become lawful in a state of necessity (idtirar). From His saying ﴿That is wickedness﴾ up to here is a parenthetical interjection (i'tiraD) that occurred in between, and its purpose is to emphasize the meaning of prohibition that was mentioned, for the prohibition of these impurities (khaba'ith) is part of the complete religion, the perfect blessing, and Islam, which is the religion approved by Allah the Exalted.

The meaning of "idturra" is: he was afflicted with a harm (durr) which makes it impossible for him to refrain from carrion. "Al-makhmasa" is hunger. The lexicographers said: "al-khamS" is the emptiness of the belly of food due to hunger, and its origin is from "al-khamS," which is the shrinking of the belly. It is said: a man is "khamIS" and "khamSan," and a woman is "khamIsa" and "khamSana," and the plural is "khamA'is" and "khamSanat."

As for His saying ﴿without inclining to sin (ghayra mutajanifin li-ithm)﴾, i.e., without intending it deliberately. Its origin in the language is from "al-janaf," which is inclination, as He the Exalted said: ﴿But whoever fears from a testator an injustice (janafan) or a sin﴾ [al-Baqarah: 182], i.e., an inclination. So His saying ﴿ghayra mutajanif﴾ means: not inclining and not deviating.

It is permissible that "ghayr" be in the accusative by an implied elided verb with the meaning: "then he partakes, not inclining..." It is also permissible that it be in the accusative by His saying "idturra," and the elided element is then delayed, with the meaning: "So whoever is compelled, not inclining to sin, and partakes, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."

The meaning of "sin" here, according to the people of Iraq, is to eat beyond satiety for pleasure, and according to the people of the Hijaz, is to be disobedient by his journey. We have thoroughly discussed this matter in the tafsir of Surat al-Baqarah in His saying: ﴿So whoever is compelled, neither desiring nor transgressing﴾ [al-Baqarah: 173].

As for His saying ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, it means: He forgives them for eating the prohibited when they are compelled to eat it, and He is Merciful to His servants in that He made that prohibited thing lawful for them when they are in need of eating it.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 5, verse 4 (part 1 of 2):

Page 112

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They ask you what has been made lawful for them. Say: "Lawful for you are the good things"﴾. This also is connected to what preceded concerning food and eatables. There are several issues in the verse.

The first issue: The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: "In the question there is the meaning of saying, so for this reason there came after it: ﴿what has been made lawful for them﴾, as if it were said: 'They say to you: what has been made lawful for them?' And He did not say 'what has been made lawful for us', as a reporting of what they said."

Know that this is weak, because if this were a reporting of their speech, they would have said "what has been made lawful for them", and it is known that this is false, for they do not say that; rather they say "what has been made lawful for us". Rather, the correct view is that this is not a reporting of their speech in their wording, but an explanation of how the event occurred.

The second issue: al-Wahidi said: "'Madha' (what): if you make it a single noun, it is in the nominative by being the subject, and its predicate is 'uhilla (has been made lawful)'. And if you wish, you may make 'ma' alone the noun, with its predicate being 'dha', and 'uhilla' is part of the relative clause of 'dha', because it means: what is it that has been made lawful for them?"

The third issue: The Arabs in the pre-Islamic period used to forbid some good things, such as the baḥīrah, the sā'ibah, the waṣīlah and the ḥām. They used to judge that these were good, but they forbade eating them on account of weak doubts. So He, exalted, mentioned that everything that is found agreeable is lawful, and He confirmed this verse with His saying: ﴿Say: "Who has forbidden the adornment of God which He brought forth for His servants, and the good things of sustenance?"﴾ [al-A'raf: 32], and with His saying: ﴿He makes lawful for them the good things and forbids for them the foul things﴾ [al-A'raf: 157].

Know that "ṭayyib" in the language means that which is pleasurable, and the permitted lawful thing is also called "ṭayyib" by way of comparison with what is pleasurable, because the two are joined in the absence of harm. So it is not possible that the intended meaning of "the good things" here is "the made-lawful things", for otherwise the sense of the verse would be: "Say: lawful for you are the made-lawful things", and it is known that this is feeble. Therefore it is necessary to interpret "the good things" as what is pleasurable and desired, so the sense becomes: "Lawful for you is everything that is pleasurable and desired."

Then know that the criterion in pleasure and being found agreeable is the people of manliness and good character, for the people of the desert find all kinds of animals agreeable to eat. The indication of these verses is reinforced by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿He created for you all that is in the earth﴾ [al-Baqarah: 29]. This requires the ability to benefit from everything on earth, but He introduced specification into that generality, saying: ﴿and forbids for them the foul things﴾ [al-A'raf: 157]. In these many verses He explicitly permitted the pleasurable and the good things, and so this became a great principle and a rule to which one returns in knowing what is lawful and unlawful of foods. Among its applications: the flesh of horses is permissible according to al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said it is not permissible. The proof of al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, is that it is pleasurable and found agreeable, and knowledge of this is necessary, and if that is so it must be lawful, by His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the good things﴾. Among them: the animal over which the name of God was not pronounced is permissible according to al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, and forbidden according to Abu Hanifa. The proof of al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, is that it is found agreeable and pleasurable, so it must be lawful by His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the good things﴾. The verse also indicates the soundness of al-Shafi'i's view in these two issues, His saying: ﴿except what you slaughter﴾. He excepted the slaughtered animal and then explained slaughter as being between the throat (labbah) and the chest. This is achieved in horses, so it must be a slaughtered animal, and therefore it must be lawful by the generality of His saying: ﴿except what you slaughter﴾. As for the animal over which the name was not pronounced, the slaughter is also achieved, because we are unanimous that if he left out the naming out of forgetfulness, it is slaughtered. That indicates that mentioning God by the tongue is not part of the essence of slaughter, and if that is so, it is possible to perform slaughter without performing the naming, so we are like you in what is found in that case; and when slaughter is achieved, it falls under His saying: ﴿except what you slaughter﴾. Among them: the flesh of domestic donkeys

Page 113

is permissible according to Malik and according to Bishr al-Marisi, and both have argued with these two verses. However, we rely in forbidding it on what is related from the Messenger ﷺ that he "forbade the flesh of domestic donkeys on the day of Khaybar."

* * *

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And what you have taught from the hunting beasts and birds of prey, training them, teaching them of what God has taught you﴾.

On this there are issues:

The first issue: In this verse there are two opinions. The first: that there is an ellipsis in it, and the sense is: "Lawful for you are the good things, and the game of what you have taught from the hunting beasts and birds of prey, training them." So the word "game" was omitted, and it is intended in the speech because of the indication of what remains, which is His saying: ﴿then eat of what they hold for you﴾.

The second: that one says His saying: ﴿And what you have taught from the hunting beasts and birds of prey﴾ is a beginning of speech, and its predicate is His saying: ﴿then eat of what they hold for you﴾. On this interpretation the speech is sound without omission or ellipsis.

The second issue: On the hunting beasts there are two opinions:

One of them: that they are the predators among birds and beasts, singular jariḥah; they were called jawāriḥ because they are gainers, from jaraḥa and ijtaraḥa, meaning to earn. God, exalted, said: ﴿those who earn the evil deeds﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 21], meaning: those who earn. They said: whatever is taken from the game and no blood flows from it is not lawful.

The third issue: It is related from Ibn 'Umar, al-Ḍaḥḥak and al-Suddi that what was caught by other than dogs, whose slaughter was not attained, is not lawful to eat. They relied on His saying (mukallibīn), saying: "Because the specification indicates that this ruling is restricted to it." But the majority held that His saying: ﴿what you have taught from the hunting beasts﴾ includes everything with which hunting is possible, such as the leopard and the predatory birds like the shāhīn, the bāshiq and the eagle. Al-Layth said: Mujahid was asked about the falcon, the hawk, the eagle, the leopard and what is hunted with of predatory beasts, and he said: "All of these are jawāriḥ." And they answered the reliance on His saying (mukallibīn) in several ways:

The first: that the mukallib is the trainer and teacher of the jawāriḥ to hunt for their owner. This name is derived from the kalb (dog) only because training is most often done with dogs, so this word was derived from it because of its prevalence in its kind.

The second: that every predator is called a kalb, and from it is His saying, upon him be blessings and peace: "O God, send upon him a dog from among Your dogs, so the lion devoured him."

The third: that it is derived from kalab, which means eagerness, as one says: so-and-so is kalib with such-and-such, when he is greedy for it.

The fourth: Grant that what is mentioned in this verse is the permission of hunting with dogs; yet specifying it by mention does not negate the lawfulness of other things, by the evidence that hunting by shooting and by setting a net is permissible, and it is not mentioned in the verse. And God knows best.

The fourth issue: The verse indicates that hunting with the jawāriḥ is only lawful if the jawāriḥ are trained, because He, exalted, said: ﴿And what you have taught from the hunting beasts and birds of prey, training them, teaching them of what God has taught you﴾. And the Prophet ﷺ said to 'Adi ibn Hatim: "If you release your trained dog and mention the name of God, then eat." Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said: The dog does not become trained except by certain matters: when it is released it runs off, when it is taken it is held back and does not eat, when it is called it answers, and when he wants it he does not flee from him. When it does this several times, it is trained. He, may God have mercy on him, did not mention a specific limit in this, but said: whenever it is predominantly thought that it has been trained, a ruling is made accordingly. He said: because if the term is not known from the text or the consensus, it is necessary to refer to custom, and this is the view of Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, in the most apparent of the reports. Al-Hasan al-Basri, may God have mercy on him, said: it becomes trained with a single time. From Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, in another report, it becomes trained by repeating this twice, and this is the view of Ahmad, may God have mercy on him. From Abu Yusuf and Muhammad, may God have mercy on them both: it becomes trained with three times.

Page 114

The fifth issue: al-Kallab and al-Mukallib is the one who trains dogs to hunt; so mukallib is one who has the act of training (taklib), like mu'allim, one who has the act of teaching (ta'lim), and mu'addib, one who has the act of discipline (ta'dib). The author of al-Kashshaf said: it was also read as mukliběn with the lightened form, and af'ala and fa'ala are very often interchangeable.

The sixth issue: The accusative of mukallibīn is in the state (ḥāl) of "'allamtum". If it is asked: what is the benefit of this state, since one is already independent of it by "'allamtum"?

We say: its benefit is that the one who teaches the jawāriḥ is skilled in his knowledge, trained in it, described as one who trains. "Tu'allimūnahunna" is a second state or a resumption, and the intended purpose of it is to emphasise the requirement of teaching.

* * *

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿then eat of what they hold for you﴾. On this there are two issues:

The first issue: Know that if the dog is trained, then it hunts a game, wounds it, kills it, and the hunter finds it dead, then it is lawful. The wound of the hunting animal is like slaughter, and likewise the ruling for all trained hunting animals. Likewise for the arrow and the spear. As for when the dog hunts it, crouches over it and kills it with its mouth without a wound, some said: its eating is not permitted, because it is carrion. Others said: it is lawful, because it falls under His saying: ﴿then eat of what they hold for you﴾. All this is when it has not eaten from it. If it has eaten from it, the scholars have differed about it. According to Ibn 'Abbas, Ṭawus, al-Sha'bi, 'Ata' and al-Suddi, it is not lawful, and this is the most apparent of al-Shafi'i's views. They said: because it has held the game for itself, and the verse indicates that it is only lawful if it held it for its owner. The indication of this is also what is related: that the Prophet ﷺ said to 'Adi ibn Hatim: "If you release your dog, mention the name of God; if you reach it and it has not killed, then slaughter it and mention the name of God over it; and if you reach it and it has killed but not eaten, then eat, for it has held for you; and if you find that it has eaten, then do not eat any of it, for it has held for itself." Salman al-Farisi, Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, Ibn 'Umar and Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with them, said: it is lawful even if it has eaten; and this is al-Shafi'i's second view. They differed concerning the falcon when it eats. Some said: there is no difference between it and the dog; if it eats any of the game, that game is not to be eaten, and this is related from 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may God be pleased with him. Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Hanifa and al-Muzani said: what remains of the birds of prey is eaten, and what remains of the dog is not eaten. The difference is that the dog can be trained to refrain from eating by beating, but the falcon cannot be trained to refrain from eating.

The second issue: The "min" in His saying: ﴿mimma amsakna (of what they hold)﴾ has two possibilities:

The first: that it is an additional particle, like His saying: ﴿Eat of its fruit when it bears fruit﴾ [al-An'am: 141].

The second: that it is partitive, and on this interpretation there are two possibilities:

The first: that the whole game is not eaten; for its flesh is eaten, but its bones, its blood and its feathers are not eaten.

The second: that the meaning is: eat of what the jawāriḥ leave for you after they have eaten from it. They said: the verse indicates that if the dog eats from the game, what remains is lawful. They said: and if it eats from the game, that does not impair that it held it for its owner, because the characteristic of holding is that it takes the game and does not leave it until it goes away, and this meaning is present whether it has eaten from it or not.

* * *

Then He, exalted, said: ﴿And mention the name of God over it﴾. On this there are sayings:

The first: that the meaning is: pronounce the name of God when you release your dog. It is related that the Prophet ﷺ said: "If you release your dog and mention the name of God, then eat." On this interpretation, the pronoun in His saying "'alayhi (over it)" refers to "what you have taught from the hunting beasts", i.e., pronounce the name over it at its release.

Page 115

The second opinion: the pronoun refers to what the (trained hunting animals) have caught, meaning: pronounce the name of God over it if you reach its slaughter (dhakah).

The third: the pronoun refers to the eating, meaning: mention the name of God over the eating. It is related that the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Umar ibn Abi Salamah: "Say 'Bismillah' and eat from what is near you."

Know that the position of al-Shafi'i (may God have mercy on him) is that the one who deliberately leaves out the tasmiyah (saying the name of God) may still eat it. If we take this verse according to the third opinion, there is no issue. But if we take it according to the first and second opinions, the command is understood as recommendation (nadb), in harmony with the texts indicating its permissibility. We will discuss this question, God willing, in the commentary on His words: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of God has not been mentioned﴾ [al-An'am: 121].

* * *

Then God, exalted is He, said: ﴿And fear God. Indeed, God is swift in reckoning﴾, meaning: beware of opposing God's command by permitting what He has made lawful or prohibiting what He has forbidden.

The Qur'an, The Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb), Surah 5, verse 5 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿This day the good things have been made lawful for you﴾.

Know that Allah the Exalted, in the previous verse, informed that He made the good things lawful. The purpose of mentioning it was to inform about this ruling. Then He repeated it in this verse. The reason for the repetition is that He said: ﴿This day I have perfected your religion for you and completed My favour upon you﴾. So He made clear that just as He perfected the religion and completed the favour in everything related to religion, He likewise completed the favour in everything related to the worldly life, and among these is making the good things lawful. The purpose of the repetition is to draw attention to this point.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿The food of those who were given the Scripture is lawful for you﴾. Regarding the meaning of "food" here, there are three views.

The first: it refers to slaughtered animals. That is, it is lawful for us to eat the slaughtered animals of the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab). As for the Magians (al-Majus), the practice regarding them is the practice applied to the People of the Book in taking the jizya (poll tax) from them, but not in eating their slaughtered animals or marrying their women. It is narrated from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he made an exception for the Christians of the Banu Taghlib, and said: "They are not upon Christianity, and they have taken from it nothing except drinking wine." This is the view adopted by al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. And it is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, that he was asked about the slaughtered animals of the Arab Christians, and he said: "There is no harm in it." This is the view adopted by Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him.

The second view: the intended meaning is bread, fruit, and whatever does not require dhabh (ritual slaughter). This is reported from some of the imams of the Zaydiyya.

The third: the intended meaning is all foodstuffs collectively. Most scholars hold the first view, and they preferred it for several reasons:

One: slaughtered animals are what become food through the act of the slaughterer. So interpreting His saying ﴿the food of those who were given the Scripture﴾ as referring to slaughtered animals is more appropriate.

Two: everything other than slaughtered animals was lawful before it belonged to the People of the Book and after it came to belong to them. So there is no benefit in specifying it for the People of the Book.

Three: what precedes this verse is about hunting and slaughtered animals, so interpreting this verse as referring to slaughtered animals is more appropriate.

[Page 116]

Then He said: ﴿And your food is lawful for them﴾. That is, it is lawful for you to feed them from your food, because it is not impossible that Allah would forbid us from feeding them from our slaughtered animals. Also, the benefit of mentioning this is that the permission of marriage is not established on both sides, whereas the permission of slaughtered animals is established on both sides. Therefore Allah the Exalted mentioned this as an indication to distinguish between the two types.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And chaste women from among the believing women﴾. Regarding "chaste women" (al-muhsanat) there are two views:

One: they are free women (al-hara'ir).

The second: they are chaste women in general, and on the second view, marriage to a slave woman is included. The first view is preferable, for several reasons:

One: after this verse He said: ﴿when you have given them their wages﴾, and the mahr (dowry) of a slave woman is not paid to her but to her master.

Two: we have explained in the interpretation of His saying: ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford to marry free believing women, then from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾ [An-Nisa' 4:25] that marrying a slave woman is permitted only under two conditions: inability to afford a free woman, and fear of falling into sin (al-'anat).

Three: restricting lawfulness to chaste women implies, apparently, the prohibition of marrying a fornicating woman, and it has been established that this is not prohibited. Whereas if we interpret "chaste women" as free women, it would require the prohibition of marrying a slave woman, and we do hold this in some circumstances.

Four: we have explained that the derivation of ihsan (chastity/marriage) is from tahassun (being protected), and the description of tahassun is more firmly established in the case of a free woman than in the case of a slave woman, because a slave woman, although chaste, is not free of going out, appearing, and mixing with people, unlike a free woman. Therefore it is established that interpreting "chaste women" as free women is preferable to interpreting them otherwise.

* * *

Then He said: ﴿And chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture before you﴾. In this verse there are several issues:

The first issue: most jurists hold that it is lawful to marry dhimmi (protected non-Muslim) women from among the Jews and Christians, and they relied on this verse as evidence. Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with both of them, did not hold this view, and he argued with His saying: ﴿And do not marry polytheistic women until they believe﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:221], and said: "I know of no shirk greater than her saying that her lord is Jesus." Those who held the first view answered the use of His saying ﴿and chaste women from among those who were given the Scripture﴾ with several points:

The first: the intended meaning is those among them who believed. For it might have occurred to some of them that if a Jewish woman believes, is it lawful for a Muslim to marry her or not? So Allah the Exalted, through this verse, made clear that this is permitted.
