and because we agreed that it must be washed before the hair grows; the hair's covering between it and the face does not remove the obligation, like the forehead: since its washing was obligatory before the eyebrow hair grew, it remains obligatory after it.
* * *
The twenty-sixth issue: Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said: it is obligatory to bring water to what is beneath a thin beard. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: it is not obligatory. Our argument is that His words, exalted is He, ﴿So wash your faces﴾ require washing the face, and "the face" is the name for the skin extending from the forehead to the chin. The application of this is abandoned when the beard is thick, in application of His words: ﴿and He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾; and when the beard is thin, this hardship does not arise, so the verse indicates the obligation of washing it.
* * *
The twenty-seventh issue: Is it obligatory to let water pass over what hangs down from the beard beyond the limit of the face, and over what extends from it sideways to the ears? Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, has two opinions on this:
One of them: it is obligatory.
The second: it is not obligatory, and this is the view of Malik, Abu Hanifa and al-Muzani.
The argument of al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, is that we agree that in a thick beard it is not obligatory to bring water to the roots of the hairs, which is the skin. We only dropped this requirement because we treated the outer surface of the beard as standing in the place of the facial skin in being the face. And if the outer surface of the beard is called a face, and the face must be washed completely, by the evidence of His words: ﴿So wash your faces﴾, then by the force of this evidence it is necessary to bring water to the outer surface of the entire beard.
* * *
The twenty-eighth issue: If a woman grows a beard, it is obligatory to bring water to the facial skin, even if that beard is thick, because the apparent meaning of the verse indicates the obligation to wash the face, and "the face" is an expression for the skin extending from the beginning of the forehead to the end of the chin. We left its application for men for the sake of removing hardship, and a woman's beard is rare, so it remains on the original ruling.
Know that it is obligatory to bring water to what lies beneath thick hair in five places: the lower lip hair (ʿanfaqa), the two eyebrows, the two mustaches, the two sideburns, and the eyelashes, because His words: ﴿So wash your faces﴾ indicate the obligation to wash all the skin of the face. Its application was abandoned in the case of thick beard for the sake of removing hardship, and these hairs are thin, so there is no hardship in bringing water to the skin, so it remains on the original ruling.
* * *
The twenty-ninth issue: Al-Sha'bi said: what faces forward from the ear is counted as part of the face and must be washed with the face, and what turns backward from it is counted as part of the head and is wiped. According to us, the ear is not at all part of the face, since the face is that which faces one, and the ear is not like that.
* * *
The thirtieth issue: The majority said: washing the two hands up to the two elbows is obligatory together with them. Malik and Zufar, may God have mercy on them both, said: washing the elbows is not obligatory. This disagreement also occurs regarding His words: ﴿and your feet up to the two ankles﴾. Zufar's argument is that the word "ila" (up to) is for the end of the limit, and what is made the limit of a ruling is excluded from it, as in His words ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾ [al-Baqarah: 187]. Therefore washing the elbows is not obligatory.
The answer is in two ways. The first: the limit of a thing may be separated from the thing limited by a perceptible break, and here the limit is outside the limited thing, as in His words: ﴿Then complete the fast until the night﴾, for the day is perceptibly separated from the night, since the separation of light from darkness is perceptible. It may also not be like this, as when you say: "I sold you this garment from this edge to that edge," for the edge of the garment is not separated from the garment by a perceptible break.
page 126
Once you know this, we say: there is no doubt that the distinction of the elbow from the forearm has no specific joint, and when that is so, assigning the washing to one part is no better than assigning it to another part, so it must be said that the washing of the entire elbow is obligatory.
The second answer: even if we grant that the elbow need not be washed, the elbow (mirfaq) is the name for what extends beyond the end of the bone, for it is the place on which one leans (yurtafaqu bihi), i.e., on which one rests. And there is no dispute that what lies beyond the end of the bone is not obligatory to wash. This answer is the choice of al-Zajjaj, and God knows best.
* * *
The thirty-first issue: If the man is amputated: if he is amputated from below the elbow, it is obligatory for him to wash what remains of the elbow, because His words: ﴿So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows﴾ require washing the two hands up to the two elbows, so when part of it falls away through amputation, the remainder must be washed by the ruling of the verse. If he is amputated above the two elbows, nothing is obligatory, because the locus of this obligation no longer exists at all. If he is amputated at the elbow, al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said: it is obligatory to let water touch the end of the bone. This is because, since washing the elbow is obligatory, and the elbow is the expression for the meeting point of the two bones, when it is obligatory to let water touch the meeting point of the two bones, it is necessarily obligatory to let water touch the end of the second bone.
* * *
The thirty-second issue: Giving precedence to the right over the left is recommended (mandub) and not obligatory. Ahmad said it is obligatory. Our argument is that He mentioned the hands and feet and did not mention giving precedence to the right over the left in it, and this indicates that the obligation is washing the two hands in any manner, and God knows best.
* * *
The thirty-third issue: The sunnah is to pour water on the palm so that the water flows from the palm to the elbow. If one pours water on the elbow until the water flows to the palm, some said: this is not permissible, because He, exalted is He, said: ﴿and your hands up to the elbows﴾, making the elbows the limit of the washing, so making it the starting point of the washing contradicts the verse, and therefore it must not be permissible. The majority of jurists said: it does not invalidate the validity of the ablution, but it is abandoning the sunnah.
* * *
The thirty-fourth issue: If two forearms and two palms grow from the elbow, it is obligatory to wash them all, because of the generality of His words: ﴿and your hands up to the elbows﴾. Likewise, if an extra finger grows on the palm, it is obligatory to wash it by the ruling of this verse.
* * *
The thirty-fifth issue: His words, exalted is He: ﴿up to the elbows﴾ require limiting the command, not limiting the thing commanded. That is, His words: ﴿So wash your faces and your hands up to the elbows﴾ are a command to wash the two hands up to the two elbows, so the obligation of washing is limited by this limit, and what remains obligatory is only this extent. As for the washing itself, it is not limited by this limit, because it has been established by reports that prolonging the whiteness (of the limbs) is a confirmed sunnah.
* * *
The thirty-sixth issue: Al-Shafi'i, may God have mercy on him, said: the obligation in wiping the head is the least thing that is called wiping of the head. Malik said: wiping the whole is obligatory. Abu Hanifa, may God have mercy on him, said: the obligation is wiping a quarter of the head. The argument of al-Shafi'i is that if one says, "I wiped the handkerchief," this is not accepted as true unless the whole of it was wiped; but if one says, "I wiped my hand with the handkerchief," this suffices for its truth by wiping the two hands with a part of that handkerchief.
Once this is established, we say: His words: ﴿and wipe over your heads﴾ suffice for acting upon it by wiping the hand over a part of the head. Then that part is not specified in the verse. If we require its specification by a definite amount, that amount cannot be determined except by evidence
page 127
other than this verse, so the verse would become ambiguous, which contradicts the basic principle. And if we say that it suffices to make the wiping fall upon any part of the head, the verse becomes clear and beneficial. It is known that interpreting the verse in a way that keeps it beneficial is better than interpreting it in a way that leaves it ambiguous, so resorting to what we have said is better. And this is a fine deduction from the verse.
* * *
The thirty-seventh issue: It is not permissible to suffice with wiping over the turban. Al-Awza'i, al-Thawri and Ahmad said: it is permissible. Our argument is that the verse indicates that wiping upon the head is obligatory, and wiping the turban is not wiping the head. They argued with what is narrated, that "he, upon him be prayers and peace, wiped over the turban."
Our answer: perhaps he wiped the required amount on the head and the remainder over the turban.
* * *
The thirty-eighth issue: People differed regarding wiping the two feet and washing them. Al-Qaffal in his tafsir related from Ibn 'Abbas, Anas ibn Malik, 'Ikrimah, al-Sha'bi and Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir that the obligation regarding them is wiping, and this is the position of the Imamiyya among the Shi'a. The majority of jurists and exegetes said: their obligation is washing. Dawud al-Isfahani said: it is obligatory to combine both, and this is the view of al-Nasir li-l-Haqq among the imams of the Zaydiyya. al-Hasan al-Basri and Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari said: the one who is obligated is given the choice between wiping and washing.
The argument of those who hold that wiping is obligatory rests on the two famous readings of His words: ﴿and your feet﴾. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, Abu 'Amr and 'Asim in the transmission of Abu Bakr from him read it in the genitive (jarr), while Nafi', Ibn 'Amir and 'Asim in the transmission of Hafs from him read it in the accusative (nasb). We say: as for the reading in the genitive, it requires that the feet be conjoined to the heads, so just as wiping is obligatory on the head, so too on the feet.
If it is said: why could it not be said that this is in the genitive by attraction (kasr 'ala al-jiwar), as in the phrase "juhr dabb kharib" (the hole of a dried-up lizard), and His words: "kabir unas fi bijad muzammal" (the great one of people in a mantle wrapped up)?
We say: this is false in several respects:
The first: the genitive by attraction is counted among the solecisms tolerated for the necessity of poetry, and the words of God must be exempted from it.
The second: the genitive by attraction is resorted to only where safety from ambiguity is achieved, as in "juhr dabb kharib," for it is known by necessity that "kharib" is not a qualifier of the lizard but of the hole. In this verse, safety from ambiguity is not achieved.
The third: the genitive by attraction occurs only without a conjunction particle; but with a conjunction particle the Arabs did not speak that way. As for the reading in the accusative, they also said it requires wiping, because His words: ﴿and wipe over your heads﴾, "your heads" is in the accusative position but is governed by the preposition "bi" (so it is in the genitive in form). So if you conjoin the feet to the heads, it is permissible for the feet to be in the accusative, conjoined to the position of the heads, or in the genitive, conjoined to the apparent form. This is a well-known view of the grammarians.
Once this is established, we say: it has become clear that the governing element of the accusative in His words: ﴿and your feet﴾ may be His words ﴿and wipe﴾, and it may be His words ﴿So wash﴾. But when two governing elements both act upon one object, the closer one taking effect is preferable, so the governing element of the accusative in His words ﴿and your feet﴾ must be His words ﴿and wipe﴾. Thus it is established that the reading of ﴿and your feet﴾
page 128
with the accusative of the lam also requires wiping. This is the way of deriving the obligation of wiping from this verse. Then they said: it is not permissible to repel this by reports, because they are all of the category of single transmission (ahad), and abrogating the Qur'an by a single report is not permissible.
Know that it is not possible to answer this except in two ways.

**The first:** The many reports (akhbar) that enjoin washing (ghasl) have been transmitted. Washing includes wiping, but wiping does not include washing. So washing is closer to caution (ihtiyat), and it is therefore obligatory to adopt it. On this view, it is certain that washing the feet takes the place of wiping them.

**The second:** The obligation for the feet is delimited by "up to the ankles" (ila al-ka'bayn), and the delimitation was stated for washing, not for wiping. The people (the opponents) answered this in two ways:

**The first answer:** The ankle (ka'b) is the bone beneath the joint of the foot. On this interpretation, wiping the upper surface of the two feet is obligatory.

**The second answer:** They grant that the two ankles are the two protruding bones on either side of the shin, but they maintain that one must wipe the upper surfaces of the feet up to these two points. In that case, this objection does not arise.

* * *

**Issue thirty-nine:** The position of the majority of jurists (fuqaha') is that the two ankles are the two protruding bones on either side of the shin. The Imamiyya (Imami Shi'a) and everyone who holds that wiping is obligatory said that the ankle is a rounded bone, like the ankle bone of cattle and sheep, placed beneath the shin bone where the joint of the shin and foot meets. This is the view of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him. al-Asma'i used to prefer this view and would say: "The two protruding ends are called al-mankibayn." This was transmitted by al-Qaffal in his tafsir.

The majority's arguments are several:

**The first:** If the ankle were what the Imamiyya say, then each foot would have one ankle, and it should have been said: "and your feet up to the ankles" (wa arjulakum ila al-ki'ab). Just as, since each hand has one elbow, He said: ﴿and your hands up to the elbows﴾.

**The second:** The rounded bone placed in the joint is something hidden, which only anatomists know. The two protruding bones at the ends of the shin are perceptible and known to everyone. The basis of general obligations (manat al-taklif al-'amma) must be something manifest, not something hidden.

**The third:** It has been reported from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Join the ankles to the ankles." There is no doubt that what is meant is what we have mentioned.

**The fourth:** The word ka'b is derived from elevation and prominence. From it comes ka'ib, a girl whose breasts have swelled, and from it ka'b for anything that rises.

The argument of the Imamiyya: The term ka'b applies to the specific bone found in the feet of all animals, so it must be so in the case of humans as well. Also, a joint is called ka'b, as in ku'ub al-rumh (the joints of a spear), and there is a joint in the middle of the foot. Therefore, the ka'b must be that.

The reply: The basis of manifest obligations must be something manifest, and what we have mentioned is more manifest. Therefore, the ka'b must be what we have said.

* * *

**Issue forty:** The majority of jurists established the permissibility of wiping over leather socks (al-mash 'ala al-khuffayn). The Shi'a and the Khawarij (Kharijites) unanimously rejected it. They argued that the apparent meaning of the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles﴾ requires either washing the two feet or wiping them. Wiping over the socks is neither wiping the two feet nor washing them. Therefore, by the ruling of this verse's text, it should not be permitted. Then they said: Those who hold that wiping over socks is permissible rely only on a report (khabar), but returning to the Qur'an is better than returning to this report. This is shown by several points:

**The first:** Abrogating the Qur'an by a solitary report (khabar al-wahid) is not permissible.

**The second:** This verse is in Surat al-Ma'ida, and the exegetes agreed that this surah contains absolutely no abrogated verse (mansukh), except the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿O you who believe, do not violate the rites of Allah﴾. Some said that this verse is abrogated. Given that, it is impossible to say that the obligation of washing the two feet is abrogated.

**The third:** If the report about wiping over socks preceded the revelation of the verse, then the solitary report would be abrogated by the Qur'an. If it were the reverse, then the solitary report would be abrogating the Qur'an. There is no doubt that the first is preferable, for several reasons:

**First:** Preferring the mutawatir (widely transmitted) Qur'an over a solitary report is preferable to the reverse.

**Second:** Acting on the verse is closer to caution.

**Third:** It has been reported from him (ﷺ) that he said: "When a report is transmitted to you from me, present it to the Book of Allah. If it agrees with it, accept it; otherwise, reject it." This requires giving precedence to the Qur'an over the report.

**Fourth:** The story of Mu'adh requires giving precedence to the Qur'an over the report.

**The fourth point, showing the weakness of this report:** The scholars differed about it. It is reported from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "For my feet to be cut off is dearer to me than for me to wipe over the socks." And from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he said: "For me to wipe over the hide of a donkey is dearer to me than for me to wipe over the socks." As for Malik, one of the two reports from him is that he rejected the permissibility of wiping over socks. There is no dispute that he was in the knowledge of hadith like the rising sun. Had he not recognized a weakness in it, he would not have said that. The second report from Malik is that he did not permit wiping over socks for the resident (muqim), but permitted it for the traveler (musafir) for as long as he wished, without any limit set.

As for al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa, and most jurists, they permitted it for the traveler for three days and nights, counted from the time of the minor impurity (hadath) after putting the socks on. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: its beginning is from the time of putting on the socks. Al-Awza'i and Ahmad said: the time of wiping is counted after the impurity. They said: this great disagreement among the jurists shows that the report did not reach the level of clear manifestation and fame. Since this is so, it is necessary to say that these opinions, having conflicted, cancel each other out. At that point, it is necessary to return to the apparent meaning of the Book of Allah, the Exalted.

**The fifth:** The need to know the permissibility of wiping over socks is a general need for all the responsible. If it were lawful, everyone would know it, and it would have reached the level of mass transmission (tawatur). Since this is not the case, its weakness is evident. This is the summary of the words of those who reject wiping over socks.

As for the jurists, they said: some of the Companions' opinion permitting it became known, and no denial appeared from the rest. This was therefore a consensus (ijma') of the Companions. This is the strongest thing that can be said about it.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Seventy of the Companions of the Messenger (ﷺ) told me that he wiped over the socks." As for Ibn Abbas's denial, it is reported that Ikrimah transmitted that from him, but when Ibn Abbas was asked about it, he said: "He lied about me." Atta' said: Ibn Umar used to differ with the people about wiping over socks, but he did not die until he agreed with them. As for Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, it is reported that Shurayh ibn Hani' said: "I asked her about wiping over the socks, and she said: Go to Ali and ask him, for he was with the Messenger (ﷺ) on his journeys." He said: "So I asked him, and he said: Wipe." This indicates that Aisha abandoned that denial.

* * *

**Issue forty-one:** A man whose two hands and two feet have been amputated: these two obligations have fallen from him, and the washing of the face and the wiping of the head remain obligatory for him. If there is no one with him to perform wudu' for him or to make tayammum for him, that also falls from him, because the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles﴾ are necessarily conditioned on the capacity to do it. When capacity is lost, the obligation falls. This is the whole of what relates to the issues concerning the verse of wudu'.

* The words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And if you are in janabah, then purify yourselves﴾. Al-Zajjaj said: its meaning is fa-tatahharu (so purify yourselves), except that the ta' is assimilated into the ta' (tu'), because they share the same point of articulation. When the ta' is assimilated into the ta', the first letter of the word becomes unvocalized, so an alif of connection (alif al-wasl) is added to it so that one can begin with it. So it is pronounced ittahharu (fa-ttahharu, written ﴿fa-ttahharu﴾ as "fattahharu" with the initial alif).

Know that when He, the Exalted, mentioned the manner of the minor purification (al-taharah al-sughra), He mentioned after it the manner of the major purification (al-taharah al-kubra), which is the ghusl from janabah. On this there are issues.

**Issue one:** Janabah arises from two causes:

**The first:** The emission of semen (al-mani). He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Water is only from water."

**The second:** The meeting of the two circumcised parts (iltiqa' al-khitanayn). Zayd ibn Thabit, Mu'adh, and Abu Sa'id al-Khudri said: ghusl is not obligatory except upon the emission of water. Our proof is his words, peace and blessings be upon him: "When the two circumcised parts meet, ghusl becomes obligatory."

Know that the circumcision of a man is the place from which the foreskin is cut off. As for the circumcision of a woman, know that her labia are surrounded by three things: an opening at the bottom of the vulva, which is the entrance of the penis and the exit of menstruation and the child; another opening above this, like the urethra of the male, which is the exit of urine alone; and the third, above the urinary opening, is the place of her circumcision, where there is a thin skin standing like the comb of a rooster. Cutting this skin is her circumcision. So when the glans disappears, her circumcision corresponds to his circumcision.

* * *

**Issue two:** His words ﴿fa-ttahharu﴾ are an absolute command, not restricted to a specific limb to the exclusion of another. So it is a command to achieve purification of the whole body in absolute terms. Also, since purification is restricted to certain limbs in the minor ablution, He mentioned those limbs specifically. Here, since He did not mention any limb specifically, it is known that this command is a command to purify the whole body.

Know that this purification is the bathing (ightisal), as He said in another place: ﴿nor [come near prayer] while in janabah, except while passing through, until you have washed﴾ [al-Nisa': 43].

* * *

**Issue three:** Rubbing (al-dalk) is not obligatory in ghusl. Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is obligatory. Our proof is that His words ﴿fa-ttahharu﴾ are a command to purify the body, and purifying the body does not require rubbing. The evidence is that when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about ghusl from janabah, he said: "As for me, I pour three handfuls of water over my head, and then I am purified." He established that purification is achieved without rubbing, which shows that purification does not depend on rubbing.

* * *

**Issue four:** It is not permissible for one in janabah to touch the mushaf. Dawud said it is permissible. Our proof is His words ﴿fa-ttahharu﴾, which indicates that he is not pure. Otherwise, it would be a command to purify one who is already pure, which is impermissible. And if he is not pure, it is not permissible for him to touch the mushaf, according to His words: ﴿None touches it except the purified﴾ [al-Waqi'a: 79].

* * *

**Issue five:** It is not obligatory to precede ghusl with wudu'. Abu Thawr and Dawud said it is obligatory. Our proof is that His words ﴿fa-ttahharu﴾ are a command to purify, and purification is achieved by bathing alone, and does not depend on wudu', as shown by the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "As for me, I pour three handfuls over my head, and then I am purified."

* * *

**Issue six:** Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: rinsing the mouth (al-madmada) and sniffing water into the nose (al-istinshaq) are not obligatory in ghusl. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: both are obligatory. [Page 131]

The argument of al-Shafi'i is the words of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him: "As for me, I pour three handfuls over my head, and then I am purified."

The argument of Abu Hanifa is the verse and a report. As for the verse, it is His words ﴿fa-ttahharu﴾, which is a command that they purify themselves, and the purification of the self is not achieved except by purifying all parts of the self. The application of this was set aside for the inner parts that are difficult to purify, whereas the inside of the mouth and the nose can be purified, so their remaining under the text is obligatory. As for the report, it is his words, peace and blessings be upon him: "Moisten the hair and cleanse the skin, for under every hair there is janabah." His words "moisten the hair" include the nose, because inside it there is hair; and his words "cleanse the skin" include the skin of the inside of the mouth.

* * *

**Issue Four:** If the hair of the head is braided, and not tied so that its parts are bound to one another, then it is considered. If that braiding prevents water from reaching the skin of the head, it must be undone. Mālik said it does not have to be undone. If it does not prevent water from reaching the skin, it does not have to be undone. Al-Nakha'ī said it must be undone. Our evidence is that His saying ﴿so purify yourselves﴾ refers to making water reach all parts of the body. If tying some hair to other hair prevents this, then that tying must be removed so that the obstacle is gone. If it is not an obstacle, its removal is not required, because the intended purpose has already been achieved and there is no need for it.

* * *

**Issue Eight:** Most scholars said there is no required order in ghusl (the full washing). Isḥāq said that one must begin with the upper part of the body. Our evidence is that His saying ﴿so purify yourselves﴾ is a command to purification in general, and that is achieved by making water reach the whole body. Once purification is achieved, it must be sufficient to discharge the obligation.

* His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you are ill, or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women﴾. In this verse there are issues:

**Issue One:** It is permissible for the sick person to perform tayammum (dry ablution with clean earth or dust), based on His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if you are ill or on a journey﴾. It cannot be said that the condition of not finding water is attached to it, because the absence of water is what permits tayammum, so there is no point in joining it to illness. His saying ﴿and you find no water﴾ refers only to the traveller.

* * *

**Issue Two:** Illness has three categories:

1. The first is when one fears harm and destruction. In this case tayammum is permitted by consensus.
2. The second is when one fears neither harm nor destruction. Here al-Shāfiʿī said tayammum is not permitted, while Mālik and Dāwūd said it is permitted. Their argument is that His saying ﴿and if you are ill﴾ covers all kinds of illness.
3. The third is when one fears an increase in the sickness or a slow recovery. Here tayammum is permitted according to the more sound of al-Shāfiʿī's two opinions, may Allah have mercy on him. Mālik and Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on them both, also held this. The evidence for it is the generality of His saying ﴿and if you are ill﴾.
4. The fourth is when one fears that a blemish will remain on some part of the body. In al-Jadīd (al-Shāfiʿī's later opinion), he said one does not perform tayammum. In al-Qadīm (his earlier opinion), he said one performs tayammum, and this is the more sound view, because it is the one that conforms to the verse.

* * *

**Issue Three:** If the illness that prevents the use of water is present in one part of the body and not in another, al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said that the person washes the parts where there is no harm and then performs tayammum. Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: if most of the body is healthy, one washes the healthy part and does not perform tayammum; if most of it is wounded, tayammum suffices. Al-Shāfiʿī's argument is taking the precautionary course. Abū Ḥanīfa's argument is that Allah, may He be exalted, made illness one of the causes permitting tayammum, and when illness is present in some of one's limbs, one is ill, so one falls under the verse.

* * *

**Issue Four:** If one applies to the place of tayammum a dressing that prevents water from reaching the skin, and removing that dressing does not risk destruction, al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: one must remove the dressing at the time of tayammum until the dust reaches the skin. Most scholars said it is not required. Al-Shāfiʿī's argument is observing caution. The argument of the majority is that the matter of tayammum rests on ease and the removal of hardship, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ (al-Ḥajj: 78). Requiring the removal of the dressing is a hardship, so it is not required.

* * *

**Issue Five:** Tayammum is permitted during a short journey. Some of our later scholars said it is not permitted. Our evidence is that His saying, may He be exalted, ﴿or on a journey﴾ is unrestricted, and there is no specification as to whether the journey is long or short. A speaker could say: since we say that both the long and the short journey are causes for the concession, because the word "journey" is unrestricted, we must also say that both mild illness and severe illness are causes for the concession, because the word "illness" is unrestricted. Also, what shows that a short journey permits tayammum is what is reported from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that he left his people and reached a place overlooking Medina. The time of ʿAṣr entered, so he looked for water for wuḍūʾ (ablution) but did not find it, and he began to perform tayammum. His freedman said to him: "Are you performing tayammum while the walls of Medina are looking at you?" He said: "Will I live until I reach it?" He performed tayammum and prayed, and he entered Medina while the sun was still bright and white, and he did not repeat the prayer.

* * *

**Issue Six:** A traveller who has water with him but fears thirst may perform tayammum, based on His saying at the end of the verse: ﴿Allah does not desire to place upon you any hardship﴾. Also, the obligation of wuḍūʾ falls from him if it would harm his property. The proof is that if he finds water only at a great cost, wuḍūʾ is not obligatory for him. So if it harms his own self, it is more fitting that it be excused.

* * *

**Issue Seven:** If one has water, but another living creature is thirsty and close to death, one may perform tayammum. That is because giving that water to the animal is obligatory, since the animal's right takes precedence over prayer. Do you not see that one may interrupt the prayer if a child or a blind person is about to drown or be burned? If that is so, then that water is like something non-existent, and so it falls under His saying: ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾.

* * *

**Issue Eight:** If one does not have water but another person has water, and one cannot buy it except at a grossly unfair price, one may perform tayammum. This is because His saying ﴿And He has not placed upon you any hardship in the religion﴾ (al-Ḥajj: 78) removes from him the burden of a grossly unfair price, and then he is like one who lacks water, so he falls under His saying ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. The same applies if water is sold at its usual price but he does not have that price, or if he has that price but needs it for an urgent necessity. But if he has the usual price and has no urgent need for it, then buying water is obligatory.

* * *

**Issue Nine:** If water is given to him as a favor, is it permissible for him to perform tayammum? Our companions said: he may perform tayammum, and it is not obligatory for him to accept that water, because the obligation of accepting a gift is burdensome. I am surprised at them. When they made this degree of hardship a cause for permitting tayammum, why did they not consider the fear of increased pain in illness a cause for permitting tayammum?

* * *

**Issue Ten:** If a bucket and rope are lent to him as a favor, most scholars said he may not perform tayammum, because the obligation in such a loan is small, and this person was able to find water without hardship. So it was not permissible for him to perform tayammum, because His saying ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾ is evidence that the permission of tayammum requires the absence of finding water.

[Page 133]

**Issue Eleven:** His saying ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself﴾ is a metaphor for answering the call of nature. Most scholars extended this to everything that comes out of the two passages, whether it is customary or rare, because of what the hadiths indicate about it.

* * *

**Issue Twelve:** Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: istinjāʾ (cleansing after relieving oneself) is obligatory, either with water or with stones. Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is not obligatory.

Al-Shāfiʿī's argument is the saying of the Prophet: "Let him cleanse himself with three stones." Abū Ḥanīfa's argument is that He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women, and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. He made wuḍūʾ or tayammum obligatory upon coming from the place of relieving oneself, and He did not make the washing of the place of impurity obligatory. That indicates it is not obligatory.

* * *

**Issue Thirteen:** Touching a woman nullifies wuḍūʾ according to al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, and does not nullify it according to Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him.

* * *

**Issue Fourteen:** The apparent meaning of His saying ﴿or you have touched women﴾ indicates that the wuḍūʾ of the one who touches is nullified. As for the nullification of the wuḍūʾ of the one who is touched, it is not derived from the verse; rather, it is derived from a report or from clear analogy.

* His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum on clean earth﴾. In this there are issues, and they are confined to two types:

One of them: the discussion of what purifying water is.

The second: the discussion of how tayammum is performed.

As for the first type, there are issues:

**Issue One:** Wuḍūʾ with heated water is permissible and is not disliked. Mujāhid said it is disliked. Our evidence is two-fold:

1. His saying ﴿so wash your faces﴾. Washing means letting water flow over the limb, and he has done this, so he has discharged the obligation.
2. He said ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. He made the permission of tayammum depend on the absence of water, and here the absence of water has not occurred, so tayammum is not permissible.

* * *

**Issue Two:** Our companions said: if water is deliberately left in the sun in a vessel, wuḍūʾ with it is disliked. Abū Ḥanīfa and Aḥmad, may Allah have mercy on them both, said it is not disliked.

The argument of our companions is what is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever bathes with sun-heated water and is afflicted with leukoderma, let him blame no one but himself." Some of our companions said this is disliked not on the basis of the Law, but on the basis of medicine.

The argument of Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him, is that He commanded washing in His saying ﴿so wash your faces﴾, and this is washing, so it suffices. Second, he has water available, so it is not permissible for him to perform tayammum.

* * *

**Issue Three:** Wuḍūʾ with the water left over from the wuḍūʾ of a polytheist is not disliked, and likewise wuḍūʾ with water that is in the vessels of polytheists is not disliked. Aḥmad and Isḥāq said it is not permissible. Our evidence is that he was commanded to wash, and he has done so; and because he has water, so he does not perform tayammum. It is reported that the Prophet (ﷺ), peace be upon him, performed wuḍūʾ from a waterskin of a polytheist woman, and ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, performed wuḍūʾ from water in a jar belonging to a Christian woman.

* * *

[Page 134]

**Issue Four:** Wuḍūʾ with sea water is permissible. ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ said it is not permissible. Our evidence is that he was commanded to wash, and he has done so. Also, the condition for the permissibility of tayammum is the absence of water, and whoever finds sea water has found water.

* * *

**Issue Five:** Al-Shāfiʿī, may Allah have mercy on him, said: wuḍūʾ with date-wine (nabīdh al-tamr) is not permissible. Abū Ḥanīfa, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is permissible while travelling.

Al-Shāfiʿī's argument is His saying ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. The Lawgiver obligated tayammum when water is absent. According to the opponent, he is permitted to abandon tayammum, indeed he is obligated to, by performing wuḍūʾ with date-wine. That would contradict the verse. If they rely on the story of the jinn, we say: it was said that it was water into which dates were steeped to remove its saltiness. Also, the story of the jinn took place in Mecca, and Sūrat al-Mā'idah is the last of the Qur'an to be revealed, so it is more fitting to regard this as abrogating that.

* * *

**Issue Six:** Al-Awzāʿī and al-Aṣamm held that wuḍūʾ and ghusl are permissible with all clean liquids. Most scholars said it is not permissible. Our evidence is that when water is absent, God obligated tayammum, and permitting wuḍūʾ with all other liquids would nullify that. They argued that His saying ﴿so wash your faces﴾ is a command to washing in its absolute sense, and making a liquid flow over a limb is called washing, as in the words of the poet:

*"How beautiful she is, when tears wash away her kohl."*

And since washing is a term for the common element between what is achieved with water and what is achieved with all other liquids, His saying ﴿so wash﴾ is then permission for wuḍūʾ with every liquid.

We say: this is unrestricted, whereas the evidence we mentioned is restricted, and applying the unrestricted to the restricted is what is obligatory.

* * *

Seventh issue: Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: water that has been discolored by saffron to a great extent may not be used for wudu. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it may be used. The argument of al-Shafi'i is that such water is not called water without qualification, so one who finds only this has not found water, and therefore tayammum becomes obligatory for him. The argument of Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, is that one who has it has found water, because water discolored by saffron is water described by a specific attribute, so the essence of water is necessarily present, and therefore its finder is a finder of water. Thus tayammum is not permitted, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾, which made the permissibility of tayammum conditional upon the absence of water.
* * *
Eighth issue: Water that has changed and become stagnant through prolonged standing is pure and purifying, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. He made the permissibility of tayammum conditional upon the absence of water, and this stagnant water is water, so tayammum is not permitted when it is present.
* * *
Ninth issue: Malik and Dawud said: water used in wudu remains pure and purifying. This is an old opinion of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. The new opinion of al-Shafi'i is that it no longer remains purifying but is pure, and this is the view of Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said in most narrations that it is impure. The argument of Malik is that the permissibility of tayammum is conditional upon not finding water, namely His saying: ﴿And you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. The one who finds used water is a finder of water, so tayammum is not permitted for him. When tayammum is not permitted, it is permitted for him to perform wudu with it, because no one distinguishes between the two cases. Also, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We sent down from the sky water, pure [tahur]﴾ (al-Furqan: 48). A tahur is one from which this act is repeated, like daHuk (one who laughs much), qatul (one who kills much), akul (one who eats much) and sharub (one who drinks much), and repetition occurs only if what is used for purification may be used for purification again.
* * *
Tenth issue: Malik said: water into which an impurity falls, without the water changing by that impurity, remains pure and purifying, whether it is little or much, and this is the view of most of the Companions and the Successors.
Page 135
Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: if it is less than two qullatayn, it becomes impure. Abu Hanifa said: if it is less than ten by ten, it becomes impure. The argument of Malik is that Allah made the absence of water a condition for the permissibility of tayammum in this verse, and one who has this disputed water is a finder of water, so tayammum is not permitted for him. The most that can be said in this matter is that this meaning exists when little water becomes changed; but we say: a general text is evidence in all cases other than the place of specification. Also, His saying: ﴿So wash your faces﴾ is a command to absolute washing, which has been left unapplied for all liquids and for little water changed by an impurity, so it remains evidence for the rest. Malik, may Allah have mercy on him, said: The reliance on this verse is further strengthened by His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Water was created pure; nothing defiles it except what changes its taste, its smell or its colour." This should not be opposed by His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "When water reaches two qullatayn, it does not carry impurity," because the Qur'an takes precedence over a solitary report (khabar al-wahid), and the explicit (manţuq) takes precedence over the implicit (mafhum).
* * *
Eleventh issue: It is permissible to perform wudu with the leftover water of a junub. Ahmad and Ishaq said: it is not permissible with the leftover water of a woman when she has been alone with it, and this is the view of al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. Our proof is His saying: ﴿And you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. The one who finds this water is a finder of water, so tayammum is not permitted for him; and when that is not permitted, wudu is permitted, because no one distinguishes between the two.
* * *
Twelfth issue: The leftover of predatory animals is pure and purifying, and likewise the leftover of a donkey. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: it is impure. Our proof is that the finder of this leftover is a finder of water, so tayammum is not permitted for him; and because His saying: ﴿So wash﴾ encompasses all kinds of water, as the establishment of these two arguments has already been explained.
* * *
Thirteenth issue: Water that reaches two qullatayn, into which a discolouring impurity falls, remains pure and purifying according to al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said it becomes impure. Our proof is that one who has it is a finder of water, so tayammum is not permitted for him; and because he was commanded to wash and has done so, and thereby discharged the obligation.
* * *
Fourteenth issue: Water into which leaves have crumbled: people have various details concerning it, but this verse indicates that it is pure and purifying so long as the name of unqualified water has not left it. In sum, this verse indicates that whenever the name of unqualified water remains, it is pure and purifying.
* * *
The second type: of the issues derived from this verse, issues of tayammum.
First issue: Al-Shafi'i, Abu Hanifa and most scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, said: intention is necessary in tayammum. Zufar, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is not obligatory. Our proof is His saying: ﴿So perform tayammum﴾, and tayammum is an expression for intending, which shows that intention is necessary.
* * *
Second issue: Al-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifa said: it is obligatory to wipe both hands up to the elbows. According to Ali and Ibn Abbas, up to the wrists; according to Malik, up to the knuckles (al-kू'ayn); according to al-Zuhri, up to the armpits.
Our proof: "yad" (hand) is the name for this limb up to the armpit, so His saying: ﴿wipe your faces and your hands﴾ would require wiping up to the armpits. We have left off applying this text to the upper arms, because we know that tayammum is a substitute for wudu, and its basis is lightness, as evidenced by the fact that in wudu four limbs must be purified, whereas in tayammum only two limbs are obligatory to purify. This meaning is confirmed by His saying, exalted is He, in the verse of tayammum: ﴿Allah does not want to place upon you any hardship﴾. So if the upper arms are not considered in wudu, then they are even less considered in tayammum. Since the upper arms have been excluded from the apparent text by this proof, the hands remain up to the elbows within it. The conclusion is that He, exalted is He, only omitted restricting the hands in tayammum to the elbows because it is a substitute for wudu, so restricting it to them in wudu makes mention of this restriction in tayammum unnecessary.
Page 136
* * *
Third issue: It is obligatory to cover both limbs entirely in tayammum. Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad reported from Abu Hanifa that if one performs tayammum over most of them, it is valid.
Our proof is His saying: ﴿wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾. "Wajh" (face) and "yad" (hand) are names for the whole of these two limbs, and this is achieved only through full coverage. It may be said: you have mentioned, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and wipe your heads﴾, that the letter "ba'" indicates partiality; so likewise here.
* * *
Fourth issue: Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: if one places his hand on the earth and no dust clings to his hand, it does not suffice. This is also the view of Abu Yusuf, may Allah have mercy on him. Abu Hanifa and Malik, may Allah have mercy on them both, said it suffices.
Our proof is His saying: ﴿wipe your faces and your hands with it﴾, and the word "minhu" (with it) indicates wiping with some of that dust, just as one who says "so-and-so wipes with the oil" conveys this meaning. We have thoroughly established this in the commentary on the verse of tayammum in Surat al-Nisa', and Allah knows best.
* * *
Fifth issue: Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: tayammum is not permitted except with pure earth, and this is the view of Abu Yusuf, may Allah have mercy on him. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is permitted with earth, sand, crushed pottery, plaster, lime and orpiment.
Our proof: it is narrated that Ibn Abbas said: "al-sa'id is earth." Also, tayammum is a purification whose meaning is not rationally understood, so it is necessary to confine it to the place the text specifies, and the detailed text came only concerning earth. He, peace and blessings be upon him, said: "Earth is the purifier of the Muslim even if he does not find water for ten years," and he said: "The earth has been made for me a place of prostration and its dust a purifier." And Allah knows best.
* * *
Sixth issue: If one stands in the path of the winds, and the winds blow dust upon him, whether or not he passes his hand over it, the apparent position of al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, is that it does not suffice. Some verifiers said it suffices, because when the dust reached his limbs and he then passed the dust over those limbs, he intended to use the good earth on his limbs, so it was sufficient.
* * *
Seventh issue: The position is that if another person performs tayammum on him, it is valid. It is said it is not valid, because His saying: ﴿so perform tayammum﴾ is a command to him to act, and this has not occurred.
* * *
Eighth issue: Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: tayammum is not permitted except after the time of the prayer has entered. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is permitted.
Our proof is His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you stand up﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾, and standing up for prayer occurs only after its time has entered.
* * *
Ninth issue: If one strikes his foot until the dust rises from it, Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is permissible for him to perform tayammum. Abu Yusuf, may Allah have mercy on him, said it is not permissible. The argument of Abu Yusuf is His saying: ﴿so perform tayammum with good earth﴾, and dust separated from
Page 137
the earth is not called good earth, so it must not suffice.
* * *
Tenth issue: Tayammum is not permitted with impure earth, because of His saying: ﴿so perform tayammum with good earth﴾, and what is impure is not good.
* * *
Eleventh issue: Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: a traveller who does not find water nearby may not perform tayammum until he has searched to the right and to the left, and if there is a valley he descends into it, and if there is a mountain he climbs it. Abu Hanifa, may Allah have mercy on him, said: if he is confident that there is no water, searching for it is not obligatory.
Our proof is His saying: ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. He made the absence of finding water a condition for the permissibility of tayammum, and absence of finding is conditional upon prior searching; this shows that searching first is necessary.
* * *
Twelfth issue: Searching is not valid except after the time of the prayer has entered. If one searches before it, he is obliged to search again after the time has entered, unless he has certainty that the situation has remained as it was and has not changed.
Our proof is His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and you find no water, so perform tayammum﴾. His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when﴾ is an expression for the entry of the time, so His saying: ﴿you find no﴾ must be an expression for not finding after the entry of the time; and not finding after the entry of the time is conditional upon seeking after the entry of the time. Thus we know that seeking after the entry of the time is necessary.
* * *
Thirteenth issue: There is no disagreement about the permissibility of tayammum as a substitute for wudu. As for tayammum as a substitute for ghusl on behalf of one in a state of janabah, it is permissible according to Ali and Ibn Abbas, and this is the view of most jurists. According to Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, it is not permissible.
Our proof is that His saying, [the phrase] either refers specifically to intercourse or includes intercourse; so it is necessary that tayammum be permitted as a substitute for ghusl, by His saying: ﴿or you have touched women, and you find no water, so perform tayammum with good earth﴾.
* * *
Fourteenth issue: Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said: one may not combine two obligatory prayers with one tayammum, even if one has not broken wudu, just as in wudu. Ahmad said: one may combine missed (fa'it) prayers, but may not combine the prayers of two times.
The argument of al-Shafi'i is His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you stand up﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and if you are junub, then purify yourselves, and if you are ill or on a journey, or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself, or you have touched women﴾.

**Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 5, verse 6 (part 7 of 7)**

The basis for deriving a ruling from it is that its apparent meaning requires a command for every ablution (wudu', the ritual washing before prayer) at each prayer if water is found, and for tayammum (dry ablution with clean earth) if water is not found. The obligation to perform wudu' on each occasion was set aside because of the action of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), so the apparent meaning of the verse remains in effect for tayammum.

* * *

**Issue fifteen:** Al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him) said: If a person does not find water at the beginning of the time for prayer but expects to find it at the end of the time, it is permissible for him to perform tayammum at the beginning of the time. Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Rather, he must delay the prayer until the end of the time.

The evidence of al-Shafi'i is His saying: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…﴾ up to His saying: ﴿and you find no water﴾. And His saying: ﴿when you rise to prayer﴾ does not mean rising to prayer itself; rather, it means the entry of the time of prayer. This indicates that at the entry of the time, if he does not find water, it is permissible for him to perform tayammum.

[Page 138]

* * *

**Issue sixteen:** If a person finds water after performing tayammum and before beginning the prayer, his tayammum is void. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari and al-Sha'bi said: It is not void.

Our evidence is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…﴾ up to His saying ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum﴾. He made the absence of finding water a condition for the permissibility of beginning the prayer with tayammum. Whoever finds water after performing tayammum and before beginning the prayer has lost this condition, so it is necessary that it not be permissible for him to begin the prayer with that tayammum.

* * *

**Issue seventeen:** If he finishes the prayer and then finds water, he is not obliged to repeat the prayer. Tawus said: He is obliged to repeat it.

Our evidence is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, when you rise to prayer…﴾ up to His saying ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum﴾. He permitted him to begin the prayer with tayammum when water is not found, and that has occurred. Therefore it is necessary that this be the means of his discharge from the obligation of the duty, because performing what was commanded is a cause for its validity.

* * *

**Issue eighteen:** If he finds water during the prayer, he is not obliged to leave the prayer. This is the view of Malik and Ahmad, in contrast to Abu Hanifa and al-Thawri. It is also the preference of al-Muzani and Ibn Shurayh.

Our evidence is that the absence of finding water requires the permissibility of beginning the prayer by the ruling of tayammum, as the verse indicates. Thus his prayer has been validly established. If he finds water during the prayer, we say: As long as he has not invalidated his prayer, he does not become able to use water; and as long as he has not become able to use water, his prayer is not invalidated. So each of the two depends on the other, which is circular, and circular reasoning is invalid. And Allah knows best.

* * *

**Issue nineteen:** If he forgot the water in his baggage, performed tayammum, prayed, and then learned that the water was present, he is obliged to repeat the prayer according to one of al-Shafi'i's two opinions, and this is the view of Ahmad and Abu Yusuf. The second opinion is that he is not obliged to repeat it, and this is the view of Malik and Abu Hanifa. The argument of the second opinion is that he is incapable of obtaining water. Just as the absence of water is a cause of incapacity to use water, forgetting is likewise a cause of incapacity. Thus it is established that when he forgets, he is incapable in this respect, so he falls under His saying: ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum﴾. The argument of the first opinion is that he is not excused for that forgetfulness.

* * *

**Issue twenty:** If his baggage is lost among the baggage, then in this case there is the disagreement mentioned, and the preferable view is that repetition is not obligatory.

* * *

**Issue twenty-one:** If he forgot that the water was in his baggage, but he searched thoroughly and did not find it, performed tayammum, prayed, and then found it, most scholars hold that repetition is obligatory, because the excuse is weak. Others said: Repetition is not obligatory, because when he searched thoroughly he became incapable of using water, so he falls under His saying: ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾.

* * *

**Issue twenty-two:** If he prayed with tayammum and then found water in a well beside him that could be used, then if he had known of it at first and then forgot it, the ruling is the same as if he had forgotten the water in his baggage. If he had never known of it at all, then if it had a clear sign, he is obliged to repeat the prayer; and if it had no sign, there is no repetition, because he is incapable of using the water, so he falls under His saying: ﴿and you find no water, then perform tayammum with clean earth﴾.

This is the summary of the discussion of the legal issues derived from this verse, and they are one hundred issues. We have written them in a place where we had none of the authoritative books of jurisprudence with us, and the heart was troubled because of the seizure of the lands of the Muslims by the disbelievers. So we ask Allah, exalted is He, to protect us from their evil, and to make our effort in deriving the rulings of Allah from the text of Allah a cause for the good deeds to outweigh the bad deeds. Indeed, He is the most worthy of hope and the most generous of those who are asked.

* His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah does not desire to make any difficulty for you, but He desires to purify you and to complete His favor upon you that you may be grateful﴾. In the verse there are issues:

**Issue one:** The verse indicates that He, exalted is He, is willing (murid), and this is agreed upon among the scholars. However, they differed on the explanation of His being willing. Al-Hasan al-Najjar said: He is willing in the sense that He is not overcome or compelled. According to this interpretation, His being willing is a negative attribute. Others said it is a positive attribute. Then they differed. Some said: The meaning of His being willing with respect to His own acts is that a motivator prompted Him to bring them into existence, and the meaning of His being willing with respect to the acts of others is that a motivator prompted Him to command them. This is the view of al-Jahiz, Abu al-Qasim al-Ka'bi, and Abu al-Husayn al-Basri from the Mu'tazila (the rationalist school). The rest said: His being willing is an attribute additional to knowledge, and this is what we have named the motivator. Then some of them said: He is willing by His essence, and this is the second narration from al-Hasan al-Najjar. Others said: He is willing by a will. Then our companions said: He is willing by an eternal will. The Basran Mu'tazila said: He is willing by a created will that does not subsist in Him. The Karramiyya said: He is willing by a created will that subsists in His essence. And Allah knows best.

* * *

**Issue two:** The Mu'tazila said: The verse indicates that the imposition of what cannot be borne does not occur, because He, exalted is He, informed that He did not place upon you any difficulty in the religion, and it is known that imposing what cannot be borne is the most severe kind of difficulty. Our companions said: Since the contrary of what is known is impossible to occur, what you have imposed upon us has also been imposed upon you.

* * *

**Issue three:** Know that this verse is a great principle, established in the Law, namely that the basic principle regarding harms is that they are not legislated. The verse indicates this, since He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And He has not placed upon you in the religion any difficulty﴾ (al-Hajj: 78). It is also indicated by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah intends for you ease and does not intend for you hardship﴾ (al-Baqarah: 185). It is also indicated by a hadith, the saying of the Prophet (peace be upon him): "There shall be no harm and no reciprocating harm in Islam." It is also indicated by the fact that the removal of harm is considered good by the intellects, so the matter must be the same in the Law, based on his saying (peace be upon him): "What the Muslims see as good is good in the sight of Allah."

As for demonstrating that the basic principle regarding benefits is permissibility, there are several points:

The first: His saying: ﴿He created for you all that is on the earth﴾ (al-Baqarah: 29).

The second: His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the good things﴾ (al-Ma'idah: 4). We have explained that what is meant by the good things is the pleasurable things and the things from which one benefits. Since these two principles are established, the deniers of analogy (qiyas) said at this point: There is absolutely no need for analogy in the Law, because every event that occurs, if its detailed ruling is mentioned in the Book and the Sunnah, then that is what is intended. If it is not so mentioned, then if it is of the category of harms, we prohibit it by the proofs indicating that the basic principle regarding harms is prohibition; and if it is of the category of benefits, we permit it by the proofs indicating the permissibility of benefits. No one may challenge these two principles with any analogy, because an analogy opposing these two principles would be an analogy set against the explicit text, and it is rejected, so it is invalid.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 5, verse 7:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey." And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾

Know that when Allah, exalted is He, mentioned this obligation, He followed it with what necessitates their acceptance and submission, and that is from two aspects:

The first: the abundance of Allah's favour upon them, which is what is meant by His saying: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you﴾. It is well known that the abundance of favours obliges the one who receives them to occupy himself with serving the Benefactor and submitting to His commands and prohibitions. In this there are two issues:

The first issue: He said ﴿the favour of Allah﴾ and did not say "the favours of Allah," because the intended meaning is not to reflect on the number of Allah's favours, but on the kind (jins) of Allah's favours, because this kind is one that no one other than Allah can bring about. Who can grant the favour of life, health, intellect, guidance, protection from calamities, and bringing one to all good in this world and the Hereafter? So the kind of Allah's favour is a kind that no one other than Allah can bestow. Therefore His saying, ﴿And remember the favour of Allah﴾, means reflecting on this type insofar as it is distinguished from the favours of others, and that distinction is that no one other than Him can bring it about. It is well known that when a favour is of this nature, the obligation to occupy oneself with thanking for it is more complete and perfect.

The second issue: His saying, ﴿And remember the favour of Allah﴾, implies that forgetting has preceded. How can forgetting it be conceived, given that it continuously and successively reaches us at every hour and moment? The answer is that, because of their abundance and succession, they have become like a customary matter, so the overwhelming manifestness and abundance of them became a cause for them to fall into the place of forgetfulness. For this very meaning the scholars who verify (al-muhaqqiqun) said: He, exalted is He, is hidden only because He is manifest. This is what is meant by the saying of those who say: Glory be to Him who is veiled from the intellects by the intensity of His manifestness, and hidden from them by the perfection of His light.

The second cause, among the causes that necessitate their being subject to the obligations of Allah, exalted is He, is the covenant with which He bound them. The mu'ahadah (covenant, mutual binding) is the pact that has been firmly established by agreement binding oneself. This verse resembles His saying at the beginning of the surah: ﴿O you who have believed, fulfil the contracts﴾. The exegetes (al-mufassirun) have several views regarding the interpretation of this covenant:

The first: that what is meant is the covenants that took place between the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and them, to hear and obey in what is loved and what is disliked, such as his pledge with the Ansar at the beginning of the matter, and his pledge with the believers in general under the tree, and others. Then He, exalted is He, attributed the covenant issued by the Messenger to Himself, as He said: ﴿Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you, they are actually pledging allegiance to Allah﴾ (al-Fath: 10), and He said: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah﴾ (al-Nisa: 80). Then He, exalted is He, emphasised that by reminding them that they had committed themselves to that, accepted those obligations, and said "We hear and we obey." Then He warned them against breaking those covenants and pacts, saying: ﴿And fear Allah. Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: do not break those covenants and do not resolve in your hearts to break them, for if that occurs to your minds, Allah knows of it, and He is sufficient as a Requiter.

The second: Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: it is the covenant that Allah, exalted is He, took from the Children of Israel when they said, "We believe in the Torah and in all that is in it." Since among what is in the Torah is the good news of the coming of Muhammad (ﷺ), they were bound to acknowledge Muhammad, peace be upon him.

The third: Mujahid, al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: it is the covenant that Allah, exalted is He, took from them when He brought them forth from the loins of Adam, peace be upon him, and made them testify concerning themselves: "Am I not your Lord?"

If it is said: according to this view, the children of Adam do not remember this covenant, so how are they commanded to preserve it? We say: when Allah, exalted is He, informed that this had occurred, the certainty of its occurrence was established, and at that point it is fitting that He commands them to fulfil that covenant.

The fourth: al-Suddi said: what is meant by the covenant is the rational and legal proofs that Allah, exalted is He, established concerning monotheism and the laws (al-shara'i'), and this is the choice of most of the mutakallimun (scholastic theologians).

The Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 5, verse 8:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm for Allah, witnesses in justice﴾. This also is connected to what precedes it, and the purpose is to urge them to submit to the obligations (taklif) of Allah, may He be exalted.

Know that the obligations, although they are many, are confined to two kinds: glorifying the command of Allah, may He be exalted, and compassion toward the creation of Allah. So His saying, ﴿be persistently standing firm for Allah﴾, is an indication of the first kind, which is glorifying the command of Allah. The meaning of standing firm for Allah is that one stands for Allah with the truth in everything that requires him to stand for it, from manifesting servitude (ubudiyyah) and glorifying lordship (rububiyyah). His saying, ﴿witnesses in justice﴾, is an indication of compassion toward the creation of Allah, and concerning it there are two opinions:

The first: ʿAṭāʾ said: He says, do not show favouritism in your testimony toward those who are dear to you and your relatives, and do not withhold your testimony from your enemies and opponents.

The second: al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that you make clear the religion of Allah, because the witness makes clear what he testifies to.

* * *

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿And let not the hatred of a people prevent you from being just﴾. That is: let not the hatred of a people move you to not be just. He intended, "that you not be just concerning them," but it was omitted because it is known. Concerning the verse there are two opinions:

The first: that it is general, and the meaning is: let not the hatred of a people move you to wrong them and transgress the limit concerning them; rather, be just toward them even if they harm you, and do good to them even if they go to extremes in causing you distress. This is a general address, and its meaning is: Allah, may He be exalted, commanded all creation not to deal with anyone except in the manner of justice and fairness, and to abandon inclination, injustice and oppression.

The second: that it is specific to the disbelievers, for it was revealed concerning the Quraysh when they barred the Muslims from the Sacred Mosque.

If it is said: On this opinion, how is it conceivable that the polytheists are wronged, when the Muslims were commanded to kill them, take their offspring captive, and seize their property?

We say: their being wronged is possible in many respects. Among them: when they manifest Islam, they are not accepted from them; among them: the killing of their young children to grieve the fathers; among them: inflicting mutilation upon them; among them: breaking their covenants. And the first opinion is preferable.

* * *

Then He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Be just; that is nearer to righteousness﴾. So He first forbade them from allowing enmity to move them to abandon justice, then He resumed and explicitly commanded them to be just, for emphasis and stress. Then He mentioned to them the reason for the command to be just, which is His saying: ﴿that is nearer to righteousness﴾. Its parallel is His saying: ﴿And that you pardon is nearer to righteousness﴾ (al-Baqarah 2:237), meaning: it is nearer to righteousness. Concerning it there are two aspects:

The first: it is nearer to guarding oneself against the disobedience of Allah, may He be exalted.

The second: it is nearer to guarding oneself against the punishment of Allah. In it there is a great warning concerning the obligation of justice with the disbelievers, who are the enemies of Allah, may He be exalted; so what is to be presumed about its obligation with the believers, who are His allies and beloved ones?

Then He mentioned the statement that serves as a promise to the obedient and a threat to the sinners, which is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾. He means that He is knowing of all that is knowable, so nothing concerning your circumstances is hidden from Him.

Then he mentioned the promise to the believers, so He said, exalted is He: ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds that for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾. So forgiveness is the removal of misdeeds, as He said, ﴿those, Allah will replace their misdeeds with good deeds﴾ (al-Furqan: 70), and the great reward is the delivery of reward. As for His saying, ﴿for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾, there are several aspects to it:

The first: He said first, ﴿Allah has promised those who believe and do righteous deeds﴾, so it is as if it was said: what did He promise them? So He said: ﴿for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾.

The second: the estimation is as if He said: Allah promised those who believe and do righteous deeds, and said to them: for them is forgiveness and a great reward.

The third: He treated His saying "promised" (wa'ada) as if it were "said" (qala), and the estimation is: Allah said concerning those who believe and do righteous deeds: for them is forgiveness and a great reward.

The fourth: that "promised" (wa'ada) falls upon the clause ﴿for them is forgiveness and a great reward﴾, meaning He promised them with this whole statement.

If it is said: why did He inform about this promise, when informing about the promised thing itself would have been stronger?

We say: rather, informing that this promise is the promise of Allah is stronger. This is because He attributed this promise to Allah, exalted is He, saying ﴿Allah has promised﴾, and the deity is the One who is capable of all that is capable of being done, knowing all that is knowable, and independent of all needs. Breaking a promise is impossible for Him, because non-fulfilment of a promise only occurs either from ignorance, where one forgets one's promise, or from incapacity, where one cannot fulfil one's promise, or from stinginess, where stinginess prevents one from fulfilling the promise, or from need. So when the deity is the One who is free from all these aspects, non-fulfilment of His promise is impossible, and so informing about this promise is more emphatic and stronger than the mere informing about the promised thing itself. Also, this promise reaches him before death, bringing him joy at the agonies of death, so those hardships become easier for him through it; and after death, through it, staying in the darkness of the grave and at the plain of Resurrection, upon witnessing those terrors, becomes easier for him.
